item.title: Lakers news: Of course Austin Reaves was hating on Luka Doncic’s ‘terrible’ half-court shot that buried Yaxel Lendeborg
item.description: William Liang-Imagn Images Lakers news: Of course Austin Reaves was hating on Luka Doncic’s ‘terrible’ half-court shot that buried Yaxel Lendeborg appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Los Angeles Lakers guard Austin Reaves couldn’t resist poking fun at Luka Doncic after his teammate buried a spectacular half-court shot against the Golden State Warriors on Opening Night. Instead of praising the difficult attempt, Reaves jokingly criticized Doncic’s decision-making even though the shot went in. “Terrible shot. There was 3.3 seconds left when he caught it. He could have got to at least 35 feet but… I didn’t want to shoot it. It was a good shot I guess,” Reaves said after the game. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) The playful criticism added another entertaining moment to a night when Doncic had already made his presence felt. Doncic, meanwhile, revealed that an exchange with Yaxel Lendeborg provided extra motivation before his remarkable attempt. “He was talking crazy. I knew that was going before I got it in my hands. I work on those,” Doncic said while discussing the half court shot. The Lakers star also explained how opponents talking trash can bring out a different side of his competitive personality. “Everybody knows when somebody starts talking, you got a different me. So that was it,” Doncic said about his interaction with Lendeborg. While Reaves’ comments were clearly lighthearted, the exchange highlighted the chemistry between the Lakers teammates. For Doncic, the improbable basket was another reminder of his confidence from long range, particularly when an opponent gives him additional motivation. And for Reaves, even a successful half-court heave apparently wasn’t enough to escape a little friendly criticism. The moment also showcased Doncic’s flair for delivering unforgettable highlights while keeping his teammates thoroughly entertained. Related: Lakers overreactions: Walker Kessler trade already worth hefty price after season opener that looked like Wilt, Shaq Related: Shaq just gave Lakers’ Walker Kessler the funniest new nickname in NBA after Wilt-like dominance

item.title: Liverpool ready to sign the next Jeremy Jacquet as €50m bid mooted
item.description: Liverpool ready to sign the next Jeremy Jacquet as €50m bid mooted Jeremy Jacquet has easily been one of Liverpool's best signings this season. Even though the Anfield outfit confirmed his deal during the January transfer window, he only just joined up with the Reds' first-team squad during their 2026-27 pre-season games. Before he proved how good he actually was, many people were questioning whether he'd have what it takes to replace Ibrahima Konate and, even though we're only seven games into the Premier League season, he seems like an instant upgrade. The way that he carries himself on the pitch and the way that he faces off with opponents has helped stabilise their back line massively. Of course, since he's only 21 years old, he's bound to make the odd mistake but, 90 per cent of the time, he's been one of Liverpool's best defenders. So, the fact that Julian Ward could be about to bring in the next version of the Frenchman to Anfield is hugely exciting. Finn Jeltsch could be Liverpool's next Jeremy Jacquet if they sign him The improvement of Liverpool's defence has been a main topic of conversation at Anfield over the last few years. And, while they seem to be in a good place now, with the contracts of Virgil van Dijk, Joe Gomez and Kostas Tsimikas all expiring in June 2027 , their entire back line could end up looking completely different by the start of next season. Obviously, with each of those three players now in their thirties, changes are going to have to be made at one point or another but, doing it all at once could be massively detrimental. This was proven last term after over £450 million was spent on new players by Liverpool who ended up finishing fifth in the Premier League. But, the fact that the Reds are now being linked with VfB Stuttgart defender Finn Jeltsch is rather exciting. Why Finn Jeltsch is the next Jeremy Jacquet Jeltsch is probably a player that most Liverpool fans won't have heard of. But, as Jacquet has shown, this isn't necessarily a bad thing. Coming to the Premier League was a massive step-up from Ligue 1 for the young Frenchman and, somehow, he's managed to become even better than he already was, This is why, Jeltsch, who currently plays for Stuttgart, would be an excellent signing for Liverpool. Supposedly, t he Reds are willing to pay around €50 million for the 20-year-old German and, from his statistics, he looks like a carbon copy of Jacquet. So, these statistics, coupled with the price that Liverpool want to pay for Jeltsch, make it feel like he could very easily become Liverpool's next Jacquet. That is, even if he is only a year younger than the former Rennes star.

item.title: Former Arsenal star Oleksandr Zinchenko returns to train at Ajax as free agent
item.description: Former Arsenal star Oleksandr Zinchenko returns to train at Ajax as free agent Ajax have confirmed that former Arsenal defender Oleksandr Zinchenko has returned to training with the club as he continues his recovery from a serious knee injury. Zinchenko’s contract with the Dutch club expired at the end of last season, but the club has allowed him to use their facilities to continue his rehabilitation. The 29-year-old Ukrainian left Arsenal in February 2026 after six years with the Premier League side. He joined the Gunners from Manchester City in 2019 and made 91 appearances for the club, notching three goals and five assists while playing as both a left-back and a midfielder. Zinchenko struggled for regular playing time during a loan spell at Nottingham Forest in the 2025/26 season. His time at the City Ground was cut short before he moved to the Netherlands to join Ajax on a short-term deal. However, his time in Amsterdam was also disrupted by injury. The Ukrainian international suffered a serious knee problem during his second appearance for Ajax against Fortuna Sittard, bringing his season to an early end. His contract subsequently expired on June 30, making him a free agent. The club confirmed on social media that the former Arsenal player had returned to training with the first-team squad. His current arrangement is not a formal playing contract, meaning he has not yet committed his future to the Dutch side. It remains to be seen whether Ajax will offer him a new contract once he has regained full fitness. For now, the priority is helping the experienced defender complete his rehabilitation and return to competitive football. His continued presence at the club also allows him to maintain his fitness while considering his next career move. Zinchenko thanked Ajax for supporting him throughout his recovery. He also thanked the club’s leadership, coaching staff and other employees for allowing him to continue his rehabilitation in Amsterdam. “I would like to say a massive thank you to Jordi Cruijff, coach Michel Sánchez and everyone at Ajax for giving me the opportunity to complete my rehabilitation and get back on track,” he said. “I’m truly grateful to everyone at the club for the warm welcome and incredible support throughout this journey. It means a lot to me.”

item.title: Brewers Provide Update On Brandon Woodruff World Series Roster Decision
item.description: Milwaukee Brewers pitcher Brandon Woodruff The Milwaukee Brewers have a decision to make on Brandon Woodruff before the World Series starts on Friday. On Thursday, Brewers manager Pat Murphy confirmed, per The Milwaukee Journal Sentinel's Curt Hogg , that the team has not made a decision yet, but that Woodruff "threw the ball well" on Tuesday, when he faced hitters for the first time since his injury. He faced hitters for the first time, pitching against Jackson Chourio, Brice Turang, Christian Yelich, William Contreras and Jake Bauers. Woodruff has missed a ton of time with a shoulder injury this year, but when he was pitching, he was very good. He was supposed to get season-ending shoulder surgery, but miraculously started healing and avoided that. He began throwing, hoping to be ready to return at some point. Looking for the perfect gift for a baseball player in your life? Check out our brand new baseball lifestyle brand! The difficult decision for the Brewers with Woodruff is the fact that the rules may not allow him to be replaced if he is placed on the roster and reaggravates his injury. The rules state that a player can be replaced on a postseason roster only if he suffers an acute, non-chronic injury or ailment, and to Murphy's understanding, Woodruff would not be able to be replaced if he is re-injured, per MLB.com's Adam McCalvy . If Woodruff is limited to a one-inning role, the Brewers would have to replace someone on the roster for him, and could be giving up some length. Chad Patrick and Kyle Harrison have been on the National League Division Series and National League Championship Series rosters, but have not pitched yet. Woodruff could easily replace one of them if the Brewers think he's ready and think the injury won't resurface. However, Patrick and Harrison can give Murphy multiple innings, and it's unclear if Woodruff can do that right now. More MLB: Should Brewers Activate Brandon Woodruff For World Series?

item.title: Predicting SEC football scores in Week 8: Texas in desperate need of win vs. Ole Miss
item.description: For the first time in a few weeks, there aren’t multiple top-25 matchups involving the SEC. But there is one in Week 8 and it involves the Texas Longhorns. Texas has dropped two in a row and the Longhorns cannot lose another if they hope to make the College Football Playoff this season . But the Longhorns will welcome in Ole Miss, which is coming off a big win against Missouri. That’s not the only SEC game to pay attention to. LSU travels to take on an Auburn team that upset Georgia last weekend. Tennessee is headed to South Carolina to take on a hungry Gamecocks team. Here is how every SEC game might play out this weekend. MORE: College Football SEC power rankings entering Week 8 No. 11 Tennessee vs. South Carolina Tennessee wide receiver Ben Petermann (35) and running back DeSean Bishop (18) celebrate after Bishop scored a touchdown against Alabama in a college football game on Oct. 17, 2026, in Knoxville, Tennessee. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) By all accounts, it should be George MacIntyre drawing another start in place of freshman Faizon Brandon on Saturday for the Vols. MacIntyre led Tennessee to a 26-10 win over Alabama last weekend, and while he’s not doing anything special, the Volunteers are winning. Shockingly, South Carolina is favored to win this game, which feels funny. The Gamecocks are coming off a bye, and they throttled Florida a week before. LaNorris Sellers is playing better football, but this will be a tough challenge against a stingy Tennessee defense. For the Vols, they not only need their defense to travel, but DeSean Bishop needs to continue to carry the load . While South Carolina is favored, got to take Tennessee on the road here. Final score: Tennessee 27, South Carolina 24 No. 7 Ole Miss vs. No. 19 Texas Oct 17, 2026; Oxford, Mississippi, USA; Mississippi Rebels quarterback Trinidad Chambliss (6) throws a pass during the first quarter against the Missouri Tigers at Vaught-Hemingway Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Petre Thomas-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) This game might be at Texas, but that meant nothing last week when Florida dominated the game. Star Colin Simmons is Doubtful to play against Ole Miss and we have no idea who will be playing quarterback for Texas. Arch Manning continues to cough up the ball late in games, and freshman KJ Lacey Jr. is getting more first-team reps . That’s a recipe for disaster for the Longhorns. Ole Miss is feeling pretty good after its 31-3 win over Missouri and the Rebels are rolling on all cylinders. While Texas is having quarterback issues, Ole Miss is not. Trinidad Chambliss remains one of the top signal-callers in college football, and while Texas has a good defense, Ole Miss will move the ball with Chambliss. Final score: Ole Miss 30, Texas 2 8 The rest of the games will be quick-hitter style: No. 18 LSU 34, Auburn 24 No. 13 Alabama 38, Texas A&M 24 Oklahoma 21, Mississippi State 17 No. 12 Kentucky 34, Vanderbilt 21 — Enjo

item.title: Troy Aikman thinks Joe Buck ‘f**ked him over’ as bombshell Greg Olsen revelation comes to light
item.description: Matthew Emmons-USA TODAY Sports. Troy Aikman thinks Joe Buck ‘f**ked him over’ as bombshell Greg Olsen revelation comes to light appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . More details have come to light about Troy Aikman and Joe Buck ’s alleged fight before the Buffalo Bills-Los Angeles Rams Monday Night Football game last week after the latter signed a massive contract extension . New reports (via Awful Announcing) provided new details about the heated moment . According to Dylan Byers of Puck News, Aikman and Buck’s relationship had been deteriorating for some time. A source claimed that the former Dallas Cowboys quarterback has become “increasingly cold, difficult, short, making comments” towards his broadcasting partner. Finally, Buck snapped before the Bills-Rams game. It escalated to a fight, during which Aikman’s attitude was that Buck “f**ked me over.” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Why Troy Aikman felt like Joe Buck “f**ked me over” with new contract Mandatory Credit: © Kirthmon F. Dozier / USA TODAY NETWORK The reason for Aikman’s harsh feelings is that Buck negotiated an early contract renewal with ESPN. According to the report, ESPN proposed that he might be paired with someone else besides Aikman next year. Buck reportedly liked the idea of being paired with Greg Olsen , who is currently with FOX as one of its analysts. Aikman felt betrayed by Buck and ESPN, and their agency, CAA, reportedly kept him out of the loop as well. When Aikman and Buck were brought to ESPN from FOX, the former Cowboys star was brought on first. Now, it’s the other way around as Aikman’s contract nears its end. Initial reports suggested that Aikman confronted Buck after learning about his contract extension. Both of their deals were set to expire after the 2026 season, which will culminate with ESPN’s first Super Bowl broadcast. He was later asked about the altercation, and he didn’t feel it was the right “time” to spill the beans. Aikman did note, however, that he will become a “free agent” after the season. He appears open to looking elsewhere for employment. Related: Rams vs. Raiders bold predictions for NFL Week 7 Related: Pat McAfee’s Monday Night Football alt cast takes monster L in debut

item.title: Joe Root creates history! Becomes first England batter to cross 8,000-run mark in ODIs
item.description: Joe Root etched his name in the record books on Thursday, becoming the first England batter to cross 8,000 runs in One-Day Internationals during the clash against Sri Lanka in the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series. The experienced right-hander reached the landmark with a fluent knock of 69 off 66 deliveries, striking eight fours. He achieved the feat in his 186th ODI innings, further underlining his consistency in the 50-over format. Root's latest innings took his career tally to 8,005 runs in 197 matches at an average of 50.66 and a strike rate of 87.83. His record also includes 20 centuries and 49 half-centuries, with a highest score of 166. Root leads England's ODI run-scoring charts Root's achievement puts him comfortably ahead of the other leading run-scorers in England's ODI history. Former captain Eoin Morgan occupied second place with 6,957 runs from 225 matches, leaving a gap of 1,048 runs between the two. Jos Buttler follows with 5,678 runs, while Ian Bell (5,416) and Paul Collingwood (5,092) complete the top five. Root also leads the group in career average and centuries, reflecting his ability to deliver substantial contributions across different stages of his career. Since making his ODI debut against India in Rajkot in 2013, Root has established himself as one of England's most dependable batters. His ability to combine consistency with the capacity to build long innings has made him a key figure in the side's batting line-up. A consistent run-scorer across formats Root's productivity has extended well beyond ODIs. In 2015 and 2016, he set consecutive records for the most runs scored by an England player across all formats in a calendar year, registering 2,228 and 2,570 runs respectively. In 2016, he also came within five runs of Michael Vaughan's England record of 1,481 Test runs in a calendar year, set in 2002. Root was appointed England's Test captain in 2017 following Alastair Cook's resignation. During the second half of that decade, he continued to make significant contributions in ODIs, scoring more than 900 runs in each of three consecutive years from 2017 to 2019. He stepped away from the 50-over format in 2020 but returned in 2023 ahead of the ODI World Cup in India. Although England endured a disappointing campaign, Root contributed three half-centuries. His latest milestone adds another chapter to an international career built on consistency and adaptability, establishing him as the first English batter to reach the 8,000-run mark in ODIs.
item.content:encoded: Joe Root etched his name in the record books on Thursday, becoming the first England batter to cross 8,000 runs in One-Day Internationals during the clash against Sri Lanka in the Pakistan ODI Tri-Series. The experienced right-hander reached the landmark with a fluent knock of 69 off 66 deliveries, striking eight fours. He achieved the feat in his 186th ODI innings, further underlining his consistency in the 50-over format. Root's latest innings took his career tally to 8,005 runs in 197 matches at an average of 50.66 and a strike rate of 87.83. His record also includes 20 centuries and 49 half-centuries, with a highest score of 166. Root leads England's ODI run-scoring charts Root's achievement puts him comfortably ahead of the other leading run-scorers in England's ODI history. Former captain Eoin Morgan occupied second place with 6,957 runs from 225 matches, leaving a gap of 1,048 runs between the two. Jos Buttler follows with 5,678 runs, while Ian Bell (5,416) and Paul Collingwood (5,092) complete the top five. Root also leads the group in career average and centuries, reflecting his ability to deliver substantial contributions across different stages of his career. Since making his ODI debut against India in Rajkot in 2013, Root has established himself as one of England's most dependable batters. His ability to combine consistency with the capacity to build long innings has made him a key figure in the side's batting line-up. A consistent run-scorer across formats Root's productivity has extended well beyond ODIs. In 2015 and 2016, he set consecutive records for the most runs scored by an England player across all formats in a calendar year, registering 2,228 and 2,570 runs respectively. In 2016, he also came within five runs of Michael Vaughan's England record of 1,481 Test runs in a calendar year, set in 2002. Root was appointed England's Test captain in 2017 following Alastair Cook's resignation. During the second half of that decade, he continued to make significant contributions in ODIs, scoring more than 900 runs in each of three consecutive years from 2017 to 2019. He stepped away from the 50-over format in 2020 but returned in 2023 ahead of the ODI World Cup in India. Although England endured a disappointing campaign, Root contributed three half-centuries. His latest milestone adds another chapter to an international career built on consistency and adaptability, establishing him as the first English batter to reach the 8,000-run mark in ODIs.

item.description: Sarah Strong #21 of the UConn Huskies shoots a free throw during the Naismith Basketball Hall of Fame women's college basketball exhibition game between the Syracuse Orange and the UConn Huskies at Mohegan Sun Arena in Uncasville, Connecticut, on October 12, 2026. It's her second time receiving the honor after also earning the recognition last fall ahead of her national player of the year sophomore campaign. Strong led UConn in nearly every statistical category last season, averaging 18.4 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.4 steals and 1.6 blocks per game. (Photo by Erica Denhoff/NurPhoto via Getty Images) (NurPhoto/NurPhoto via Getty Images) The reigning national player of the year begins her junior season with UConn women's basketball once again among the top returning players in the nation. Sarah Strong was named to the five-player preseason AP All-America team Thursday. It's her second time receiving the honor after also earning the recognition last fall ahead of her national player of the year sophomore campaign. The forward is joined on this year's preseason All-America team by Notre Dame's Hannah Hidalgo, USC's JuJu Watkins, Texas' Madison Booker and Vanderbilt's Mikayla Blakes. Strong was the only player to receive a vote from all 30 AP voters. Hidalgo and Booker received 28 votes, Blakes 27 and Watkins 26. Strong became UConn's sixth consensus player of the year last year, including earning the 2026 AP Player of the Year award. She was also a 2026 AP First Team All-American and a 2025 AP Second Team All-American. Strong led UConn in nearly every statistical category last season, averaging 18.4 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.4 steals and 1.6 blocks per game. Meet AP's 2026 All-America women's college basketball team, featuring JuJu Watkins, Mikayla Blakes, Hannah Hidalgo, Sarah Strong and Madison Booker. #Basketball #WomensBasketball #CollegeBasketball https://t.co/ZIww2asgsA - The Associated Press (@AP) October 22, 2026 She begins her junior year ready to take on a bigger leadership role for the Huskies as they enter a post- Paige Bueckers - Azzi Fudd era. While Strong took the summer off from basketball to rest her Achilles, she spent the offseason and preseason working to become a more vocal leader. During Monday's exhibition against Texas, the junior was seen grabbing her teammates together for impromptu huddles on the court and pulling aside each one to talk through plays, especially after something went wrong. "I think Sarah did a great job today of being that vocal presence for us, kind of being that voice we could turn to," said senior guard Ashlynn Shade. "She calmed us. She got us through the ups and downs, and that's something that I think a lot of us look to. And she's doing a great job at it." If Strong can elevate her game to the next level, she has the chance to become UConn's first player to win back-to-back national player of the year awards since Breanna Stewart won three straight from 2014 to 2016. Including Stewart, only three Huskies have been named national player of the year in consecutive seasons (others are Diana Taurasi and Maya Moore). Watkins, Booker and Blakes are Strong's biggest competitors for the 2027 award. Blakes was a 2026 Naismith Trophy finalist (along with Strong, Fudd and UCLA's Lauren Betts), while Booker was a 2026 Wooden Award finalist (also along with Strong, Fudd, Betts and Blakes). Strong won both awards on top of also winning the 2026 Wade Trophy, the 2026 USBWA Player of the Year award and the 2026 Big East Player of the Year award. Booker and Hidalgo (the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year) are seniors, while Blakes is a junior. Watkins was the 2025 national player of the year before missing the entire 2025-26 season due to an ACL injury. The USC star is expected to be the No. 1 pick in the 2027 WNBA Draft; however, she has an extra year of eligibility and could decide to hold off on declaring until 2028. UConn begins the 2026-27 season on Nov. 2, hosting Cornell. item.title: Fifa increases preparation money for Women’s World Cup to match men’s teams
item.description: Funds for 2027 will match men’s World Cup in 2026 Players given better flights and individual hotel rooms Teams in the 2027’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil will receive the same preparation money from Fifa as those that played at the 2026 men’s tournament, the world’s governing body has announced. The preparation money for the 32 teams has been more than doubled to $2.5m (£1.86m) each. In 2023, the total preparation money for the tournament was $31m; it will now be $80m. Continue reading...

item.title: Sam Hauser seems unworried about rough Boston Celtics start, bigs chemistry
item.description: While many Boston Celtics fans are stressing out over how the team dropped a 22-point lead to lose to the Detroit Pistons on Opening Night, the players on the team seem less concerned despite the familiar collapse. We can count vet forward Sam Hauser among them, who said as much following Celtics practice on Thursday (Oct. 22). "I don't think it's concerning," said the Virginia alum via CLNS Media. It's the first game of 82. "So there's definitely going to be kinks that we're going to have to work out. And obviously we ran into a few things last game. But I don't think we're concerned. I think we showed flashes of being really, really good and then flashes of areas where we need to improve." "I think that's the battle you go through each and every season," added the Celtics sharpshooter. As to what went wrong in Game 1 of 82, he said "they picked up the pressure a little bit. We didn't handle it necessarily too well, (and should) execute a little bit better on offense and then rebounding at the end of the day is always important." That rebounding was especially hurt by Boston's two best bigs, Neemias Queta and Mitchell Robinson, combining for just 7 boards. At least to start the season, their chemistry with the team seems off, which Hauser deemed important. "I think they're so involved in what we do," he said. "Setting off ball screens, running the floor ... rolling the rim hard, protecting the rim on the other end. They do a lot for us and when they're at their best, then usually we're at our best too. So we put a lot on them and they can handle it. But it's not always an easy job. But those two and Luka (Garza) as well are cut out for it." Listen to "What went wrong in the Celtics Opening Night loss to the Pistons" on Spreaker. item.title: Doris Burke tells tale of time she had Spurs legend Gregg Popovich steaming mad over Shaq
item.description: Rob Gray-Imagn Images Doris Burke tells tale of time she had Spurs legend Gregg Popovich steaming mad over Shaq appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . ESPN commentator Doris Burke recalled an embarrassing encounter with former San Antonio Spurs head coach Gregg Popovich involving Shaquille O’Neal during Wednesday night’s broadcast of the Los Angeles Lakers’ 127-105 victory over the Golden State Warriors . Burke shared how one of her earliest in-game interviews with Popovich went wrong after she questioned the Spurs’ defense against O’Neal, who had dominated San Antonio following a difficult opening quarter. “My first interview when we put interviews in to end a quarter, it’s San Antonio and Shaq had a bad quarter. But then he comes out against San Antonio and he’s like 6-for-6. And I say remarkably, unintelligently, I think my question was something like Pop, what was the problem with your defense?” Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) According to Burke, Popovich’s reaction immediately made her regret asking the question. “And I kid you not Pop just stared at me his face got very red. I don’t remember what he said. I remember getting back to my position and the producer saying Doris, do you mind if we don’t run that? And I said, thank you for not embarrassing me.” Doris Burke with a funny Pop story: "My first interview when we put interviews in to end a quarter, it's San Antonio and Shaq had a bad quarter. But then he comes out against San Antonio and he's like 6-for-6. And I say remarkably, unintelligently, I think my question was… — Oh No He Didn't 🤯 (@ohnohedidnt24) October 22, 2026 Doris Burke’s Shaq story highlights Gregg Popovich’s fiery Spurs legacy The exchange reflected Popovich’s reputation for delivering blunt responses during sideline interviews throughout his coaching career. Popovich spent 29 seasons leading San Antonio, winning five NBA championships and establishing himself as one of the most successful coaches in league history. His battles against O’Neal, particularly during the Lakers’ championship runs in the early 2000s, helped define one of the Western Conference’s most prominent rivalries. Meanwhile, the Spurs have entered a new era under head coach Mitch Johnson following Popovich’s departure from the sidelines. San Antonio opened the 2026-27 regular season with a 116-104 loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder on Tuesday night. The Spurs will attempt to secure their first victory of the season when they host the Houston Rockets (1-0) on Friday at 9:30 p.m. ET on Prime Video. Related: 3 San Antonio Spurs bold season predictions as Victor Wembanyama plots revenge for NBA Finals loss Related: Spurs Opening Night overreactions: Pump the brakes on Victor Wembanyama’s coronation

item.title: Fantasy Football Injury Impact: Breece Hall Returns To Practice, Sending Braelon Allen's Week 7 Value Into Question
item.description: New York Jets running back Breece Hall (20) warms up during a preseason opening game between the New York Jets and Tampa Bay Buccaneers on Friday, Aug. 14, 2026, at MetLife Stadium in East Rutherford, NJ. | USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect New York Jets running back Breece Hall was back on the practice field on Thursday for the first time since injuring his quad in Week 3. It is likely he returned in a limited capacity; however, we do not yet have an official designation. Breece Hall (quadriceps) was "stretching with the rest of the team" at the start of Thursday's practice. Via @antwanstaley pic.twitter.com/WNG7R8X0UY - RotoWire Fantasy Football (@RotoWireNFL) October 22, 2026 This does not guarantee that he will play this week, but it's a huge step in the right direction. Braelon Allen has filled in admirably as the lead back in New York while Hall has been sidelined. Fantasy Impact RB Breece Hall, New York Jets Getting back on the practice field is a great sign for Hall. We don't know if he'll be able to play this week, but this at least gives him a shot at being active on Sunday. At the very least, it appears that he should be able to go in Week 8 if he can't play in Week 7, barring any setbacks. If Hall is active in Week 7, he is a must-start option against the Miami Dolphins, who are allowing the second-most fantasy points to running backs this season. However, there should be some concern about Allen cutting into his workload after playing so well in his absence. Quad injuries also come with the risk of re-injury, which could cause the Jets to ease him back into action. RB Braelon Allen, New York Jets Allen is a fantastic start this week if Hall is out, but becomes very risky if Hall plays. His full workload will likely be cut to single-digit carries if Hall is active. Even in a great matchup, that might not be enough volume in the Jets' offense. We view Allen as a must-start running back if Hall is out; nevertheless, he's a risky flex option at best if Hall is out there. item.title: Mullins hit by fresh injury concerns at Newport
item.description: [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Injuries are beginning to take a toll on League Two side Newport County, with Tanatswa Nyakuhwa and Matty Jacob the latest names added to a growing casualty list. Striker Christian Doidge and midfielder Aaron Lewis both picked up groin injuries ahead of Newport's 1-1 draw with York City, while Harri Pugh and Keenan Patten also remain sidelined. With a big squad, manager Hayden Mullins feels for now Newport have the squad depth to survive the crisis but admits Jacob's absence will be keenly felt. The Hull City loanee, who arrived on deadline day, has started every League Two game since his arrival before being forced off with a hamstring strain against York. Alongside helping shore up Newport's defence, he has also posed a threat going forward and contributed two assists in seven appearances. "Matty's done really well," said Mullins. "He's a player who has shown he wants to come and play games. He recognised he needed to play, came down here and backed himself. "He's got a couple of assists and looked really good in the games. He will definitely be a miss, but it opens the door for someone else." That player could well be Tom Davies, who is fit again after recovering from an injury that has kept him out of the team since Newport's 5-3 derby defeat to Bristol Rovers. But both Joe Thomas and Alfie Merritt also remain options for Mullins, both of whom started in south Yorkshire earlier this week. "Tom [Davies] is fit now, Alfie Merritt's around and JT [Joe Thomas] can fill that position," Mullins added. "We've got a number of players that can help while he's not here [for three or four weeks], but Matty's done really well while he's been in the team." There was, however, some positive news on the injury front, with James Crole and Moses Walker-Alexander both back in training. Doidge and Lewis have also returned to the grass but are still several weeks away from contention, while Nyakuhwa is awaiting a scan to determine the extent of his injury. "We're getting there, but we're taking a bit of a knock at the moment," said Mullins. "We're stretched and that's why when the Shaq [Gwengwe] one came through it was a little bit more of a blow." With Newport now facing a testing spell, Mullins has challenged those on the fringes of the squad to take their opportunities. "I've got no worries about putting players in. If a space opens up, they'll get the opportunity because they've shown they're ready to go. "It's hard to leave people out because the lads who've got the shirt have done really well, but it's pleasing to see others come in and show us they're ready. "We're getting lads who need to step up, stepping up at the moment and that's really helping us." Newport travel across the River Severn to face Cheltenham Town on Saturday 24 October where they will be hoping for their first league away win. Though a fourth consecutive draw on the road would still extend their unbeaten run to 10 matches in all competitions.

item.title: 'I would have been moved to the left!' - Luis Figo admits he might have lost his spot to Barcelona sensation Lamine Yamal
item.description: Valencia CF v FC Barcelona - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Luis Figo has heaped immense praise on Lamine Yamal, joking that he would have been forced to change positions if they played in the same era. The legendary Portuguese winger shared his admiration for the teenager while reflecting on the differences between modern football and his own early days at Barcelona. High praise from a legend Figo has openly expressed his deep admiration for the current Barcelona sensation Yamal . The legendary winger has been closely watching the rapid rise of the Spanish international over recent months. Speaking to Betfair , Figo playfully admitted that Yamal's immense talent would have directly impacted his own role on the pitch. He revealed that he would have gladly shifted out of his favoured position just to accommodate the youngster in the same team. Making way on the wing Figo operated primarily on the right flank throughout his illustrious career at the highest level. However, he fully believes Yamal's current ability would have forced a major tactical rethink if they had ever shared a dressing room. "If we had played together, maybe I would have had to play on the left and change position," Figo explained. Despite delivering such heavy praise, the Portuguese icon was quick to remind everyone of his own exceptional abilities on the ball. "I had incredible talent, eh?" he added with a smile. FBL-ESP-LIGA-BETIS-BARCELONA Navigating a different era Yamal has managed to establish himself as a regular starter while still a teenager, but Figo faced a completely different reality. The retired star was eager to point out the contrasting landscapes of European football across their respective generations. "Times are different now," Figo reflected when comparing his own early career to the current Blaugrana prodigy. "When I arrived at Barcelona, I was barely 22 years old. I was very young, and only three foreigners could start. I didn't start playing that much. They were different times. "What I do believe is that I could be a starter for either team. If I were the coach of either side, I’d put myself in the lineup. I can’t say anything else… if I don’t say it myself, no one else will!" Getting ready for El Clasico This season, Yamal has been sensational for the Blaugrana. In 12 appearances across all competitions, the 19-year-old has recorded ten goals and ten assists. Now, the Spanish international will look to contribute once again for his team when they face Real Madrid in El Clasico this weekend.

item.title: Report: Evan Stewart's license was suspended at time of DUII arrest
item.description: Oregon football wide receiver Evan Stewart 's driver's license was suspended for missing multiple traffic violation court dates at the time of his DUII arrest Oct. 18 . According to a a report by Lookout Eugene-Springfield , Stewart's license was suspended as of March 31 because he failed to appear in Coburg Municipal Court for a speeding violation. Stewart's driving record, obtained by Lookout, indicates he drove 83 miles per hour in a 65 MPH zone on Nov. 26, 2025. Stewart also failed to appear in Eugene Municipal Court after an illegal window tint charge Dec. 24, 2025, per the driving record. The Eugene case lists a second license suspension starting April 30. Eugene Municipal Court records also show Stewart failed to carry vehicle registration and both cases are in "collections." At 5 a.m. Oct. 18, following the Ducks' 17-14 victory over the Nebraska , Stewart was stopped by Springfield police on Highway 126 near Mohawk Boulevard. The Springfield officer suspected impairment and began a DUII investigation and arrested Stewart. Oregon football coach Dan Lanning spoke about Stewart's arrest during his Monday press conference and addressed other unsubstantiated rumors involving other players associated around that night. "There's an incident this weekend that didn't match our standard here in our program," Lanning said. "There will be appropriate action taken. We're still gathering some details with what that situation looks like, but that'll be handled internally. I'm not going to respond to any other questions about that, gonna handle that with our guys. "There's an expectation of how you have to act and how you need to perform in our program and it overshadows the success that we had on Saturday, which is disappointing. But that will be handled by us internally and it's not something I'm going to speak on publicly." Stewart did not play in Oregon's win against Nebraska Oct. 17 and is listed as out on Oregon's availability report ahead of the Ducks ' game versus Illinois. Oregon tight end Jamari Johnson ticketed for speeding on the same night as Stewart's arrest Roughly an hour before Stewart's arrest in Springfield, tight end Jamari Johnson was cited for a speed limit violation at 3:51 a.m. in Springfield, per online court records. The case number for Johnson's citation matches that of a separate high-speed pursuit Springfield police are investigating, but neither Johnson or Stewart are believed to be suspected drivers in that case, Springfield police told The Oregonian. "He was not involved in the high-speed pursuit," Springfield police deputy chief George Crolly said of Johnson to The Oregonian. "We are still seeking the drivers in that case. He was stopped well before Mr. Stewart's arrest, so he was not part of the group of cars that were in the area when Mr. Stewart was stopped." But that will be handled by us internally and it's not something I'm going to speak on publicly." Stewart did not play in Oregon's win against Nebraska Oct. 17 and is listed as out on Oregon's availability report ahead of the Ducks ' game versus Illinois. Oregon tight end Jamari Johnson ticketed for speeding on the same night as Stewart's arrest Roughly an hour before Stewart's arrest in Springfield, tight end Jamari Johnson was cited for a speed limit violation at 3:51 a.m. in Springfield, per online court records. A high-speed chase involving police occurred around 3:51 a.m. Sunday, according to police dispatch logs. Shortly after an abandoned vehicle from the chase was found, Stewart was pulled over and arrested for DUII around 5 a.m. Springfield PD told The Oregonian that a group of Oregon football players left the nearby area when police discovered the vehicle. Currently, no Oregon football players have been named suspects in the case. Johnson's citation lists a $440 fine and does not disclose how fast Johnson was traveling over the speed limit. item.title: Liverpool increasingly likely to pay €55 million for Ronald Araujo as Barcelona loanee impresses
item.description: Liverpool increasingly likely to pay €55 million for Ronald Araujo as Barcelona loanee impresses According to MARCA , Liverpool are increasingly likely to consider a permanent deal for Ronald Araujo if the Barcelona defender maintains his impressive form at Anfield. A €55 million purchase option exists in the loan agreement between the two clubs giving Andoni Iraola’s side the chance to secure his services next summer on a permanent basis. The Uruguay international has adapted quickly to life in England, and his performances have strengthened the case for keeping him beyond his season-long loan. Andoni Iraola getting the best out of Ronald Araujo Araujo has made an encouraging start to his Liverpool spell after being moved from his preferred centre-back position to right-back. His physical strength and defensive aggression have helped him adapt to the demands of the role, while his attacking contributions have added another dimension to his game – he was on target in Liverpool’s recent win over Villarreal . Araujo has been doing well at Liverpool. (Photo by Stu Forster/Getty Images) Iraola has also recognised the defender’s experience and versatility, seeing both as valuable assets for his squad. “Ronald needed this change and has arrived with humility. He is an experienced player from a big club who is ready to play in different positions,” the Liverpool manager said. That adaptability could prove important when Liverpool assess whether to turn the loan into a permanent transfer. Araujo happy at Liverpool but remains cautious about his future The defender has made no secret of his satisfaction with his new surroundings. Having struggled for consistent playing time at Barcelona, Araujo is now getting the opportunity to establish himself in a new league and demonstrate his value. “I think I am finding what I needed here, which was to play, feel important and show my football. It is very early to talk about these things. I am getting playing time, which is what I want, and then we will see what happens in the future,” Araujo said. His comments reflect a desire to focus on performances rather than rush into a decision about his long-term future. Taking things one step at a time. (Photo by Kate McShane/Getty Images) For Liverpool, the priority will be to determine whether his current form can be sustained throughout the campaign before committing a significant transfer fee. Barcelona could use the €55 million to strengthen their defence Barcelona will be watching Araujo’s progress closely. The purchase option would provide the Catalan club with a substantial potential return next summer, allowing them to consider reinvesting in an experienced defender to complement a relatively young back line. However, it all depends on Liverpool’s decision on whether the €55 million outlay represents good value over the long term for them. item.title: Bruno Fernandes' $5.4 million mansion burgled by masked gang while away with Manchester United
item.description: Manchester United captain Bruno Fernandes' mansion was reportedly burgled on Wednesday -Credit:DeFodi Images, DeFodi Images via Getty Images Bruno Fernandes returned from Manchester United's humiliating loss to Como on Wednesday to discover that his home had been targeted by burglars. Fernandes grabbed attention on Wednesday for publicly criticizing United manager Michael Carrick 's tactical approach following their 4-1 demolition in northern Italy. The misery on the field was then compounded by devastating news from back home. The United captain's £4 million ($5.4 million) mansion in Cheshire was broken into by three masked individuals on Wednesday. His residence in Nether Alderley was targeted by the thieves at 8.30pm local time. Bruno Fernandes questions Manchester United staff's tactics after defeat to Como Ex-Liverpool boss Jürgen Klopp still grieving Diogo Jota's death in new biography -Credit:Robbie Jay Barratt - AMA, Getty Images As first reported by The Sun , one of Fernandes' neighbors alerted police after noticing three suspicious individuals nearby. It is believed they climbed over the backyard fence, which borders woodland, before fleeing with stolen valuables. The intruders managed to escape, despite the property being equipped with an advanced security system featuring alarms, CCTV, and an electric gate. It remains unclear whether Fernandes' partner, Ana Pinho, and their two young children were present in the house at the time of the break-in. Mirror Football have contacted Fernandes' representatives and Manchester United to request comment. A Cheshire Police spokesperson said: "At around 8.30pm on Wednesday 21 October, police were called to reports of suspicious activity at an address in the Alderley Park area of Nether Alderley. "The caller reported three unknown men in the rear garden of a neighbouring property. Officers attended the scene and on arrival there was no trace of the suspects. However, officers discovered that there had been a burglary at the address and a number of items had been stolen." To listen to the latest episode of 'All Out Soccer' - CLICK HERE Detective Inspector David Jarvis, of Macclesfield Proactive CID, added: "This investigation is in its early stages at this time, and we're committed to doing all we can to trace the people responsible. "As part of our enquiries, we're keen to hear from anyone who was in the local area at the time and believes they may have witnessed anything suspicious." The incident occurred while Fernandes was away in Como, featuring in a dismal loss. United were hammered 4-1, prompting Fernandes to publicly criticize Carrick's approach and accuse the club of being rooted in the past . United return to action against AFC Bournemouth at Old Trafford on Sunday, with Carrick facing mounting pressure to deliver a positive result.

item.title: Kompany backs Lennart Karl to rediscover best form at Bayern
item.description: Kompany backs Lennart Karl to rediscover best form at Bayern The 18-year-old has found opportunities harder to come by in recent weeks after an impressive breakthrough campaign last season. Karl was once again named among the substitutes for Bayern’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal, despite Michael Olise being unavailable through suspension. Speaking after the match, Kompany acknowledged that Karl is yet to return to the level he reached last season but stressed that the youngster continues to enjoy the full backing of the coaching staff. “The rhythm and performances will come. He’s not performing at the level he had last season, but that’s also okay,” Kompany explained. “He knows that it happens, he knows we’re patient with him. At some point his moment will come and he will show us the Lennart Karl that we all know.” Injury setback has disrupted Karl’s progress Karl enjoyed a remarkable rise last season, establishing himself as one of Bayern’s most exciting young talents thanks to his technical ability, direct attacking approach and eye for goal. However, a serious muscle injury sustained in June disrupted his progress and ruled him out of the 2026 World Cup. The forward subsequently spent around 12 weeks on the sidelines before returning to action towards the end of August. Since his comeback, Karl has been working to regain his match sharpness and the form that made him such an important option for Kompany during his breakthrough campaign. The Bayern coach acknowledged that the youngster’s injury problems have played a role in his current situation, urging patience rather than expressing concern over his development. “He’s still young, he had a few injuries. It will come, I’m not worried,” Kompany added. Competition for places remains fierce at Bayern Karl’s return to full fitness has coincided with considerable competition for attacking positions at the Allianz Arena. Bayern boast several established options in the forward line, including Olise, Luis Díaz, Serge Gnabry and Jamal Musiala, while new arrival Ismail Saibari has further increased the depth available to Kompany. Consequently, Olise’s absence against Arsenal did not automatically guarantee Karl a place in the starting XI, underlining the challenge facing the youngster as he looks to re-establish himself in the team. Nevertheless, Kompany’s latest comments suggest that Bayern are not prepared to rush Karl back to his previous level. Instead, the Belgian appears willing to give the teenager the necessary time to regain his confidence and sharpness. For Karl, the immediate priority will be to make the most of his opportunities as he looks to force his way back into Bayern’s starting lineup. Despite the current difficulties, Kompany remains convinced that the youngster can return to his previous level, with Bayern continuing to place considerable faith in one of their most promising attacking talents.

item.title: What next for Australia after chastening defeat by South Africa?
item.description: Australia were beaten by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha [Getty Images] Second Test, Gqeberha (day five of five) South Africa 425-9 dec: Bavuma 179, Jansen 85; Boland 5-81 Australia 99 & 295: Head 121; Rabada 4-77, Mulder 3-64 South Africa won by an innings and 31 runs Scorecard Some Test defeats feel more consequential than others. Some can be brushed aside as a bad day. Others point to issues that run deep. For Australia, this capitulation on the Cape feels like the latter. In losing to South Africa by an innings and 31 runs, Australia surrendered their lead in the series with one match to play. There was fight on day five: Travis Head scored 121 and nightwatchman Scott Boland survived for 166 balls to take the match into the final session, but Pat Cummins' side still had to follow-on for only the third time this century and lost in little more than three days' play around the rain. The momentum built in Durban has been swept away. "It is not just this Test," said former Australia bowler Jason Gillespie on ABC Grandstand. "We are talking about the batting and a lack of options and performance. Something will change." 'McDonald is getting impatient' It is, of course, little more than a week since South Africa were the ones facing these questions. They made three changes after Australia won the first Test in Durban. Eyes are now on the tourists' selectors and this series coming before contests against New Zealand, India and England only adds extra intrigue. A stony-faced Australia coach Andrew McDonald refused to be drawn on potential changes on Wednesday, but hardly gave ringing endorsements of his batters. "I can't defend that," McDonald said of Australia's first-innings collapse to 99 all out. Attracting the most attention is number three Marnus Labuschagne, who has gone 47 innings without an international century to equal the Australia record. His inexplicable second-innings dismissal, when he hit spinner Simon Harmer to long-on for 39 as Australia tried to save the Test, was the fourth time he has fallen in the thirties in six innings since the Ashes. "Some of the hardest part of batting at number three is getting in," said Cummins, when asked to guarantee whether Labuschagne will keep his place. "He is doing that. We need to turn those 30s into bigger scores. He knows that." In that run of wasted starts, Labuschagne has been bowled missing a flick to leg, missed another to be pinned lbw, drove a spinner straight to cover and whacked another to long-on. item.content:encoded: Australia were beaten by an innings and 31 runs in Gqeberha [Getty Images] Second Test, Gqeberha (day five of five) South Africa 425-9 dec: Bavuma 179, Jansen 85; Boland 5-81 Australia 99 & 295: Head 121; Rabada 4-77, Mulder 3-64 South Africa won by an innings and 31 runs Scorecard Some Test defeats feel more consequential than others. Some can be brushed aside as a bad day. Others point to issues that run deep. For Australia, this capitulation on the Cape feels like the latter. In losing to South Africa by an innings and 31 runs, Australia surrendered their lead in the series with one match to play. There was fight on day five: Travis Head scored 121 and nightwatchman Scott Boland survived for 166 balls to take the match into the final session, but Pat Cummins' side still had to follow-on for only the third time this century and lost in little more than three days' play around the rain. The momentum built in Durban has been swept away. "It is not just this Test," said former Australia bowler Jason Gillespie on ABC Grandstand. "We are talking about the batting and a lack of options and performance. Something will change." 'McDonald is getting impatient' It is, of course, little more than a week since South Africa were the ones facing these questions. They made three changes after Australia won the first Test in Durban. Eyes are now on the tourists' selectors and this series coming before contests against New Zealand, India and England only adds extra intrigue. A stony-faced Australia coach Andrew McDonald refused to be drawn on potential changes on Wednesday, but hardly gave ringing endorsements of his batters. "I can't defend that," McDonald said of Australia's first-innings collapse to 99 all out. Attracting the most attention is number three Marnus Labuschagne, who has gone 47 innings without an international century to equal the Australia record. His inexplicable second-innings dismissal, when he hit spinner Simon Harmer to long-on for 39 as Australia tried to save the Test, was the fourth time he has fallen in the thirties in six innings since the Ashes. "Some of the hardest part of batting at number three is getting in," said Cummins, when asked to guarantee whether Labuschagne will keep his place. "He is doing that. We need to turn those 30s into bigger scores. He knows that." In that run of wasted starts, Labuschagne has been bowled missing a flick to leg, missed another to be pinned lbw, drove a spinner straight to cover and whacked another to long-on. "I got the feeling last night Andrew McDonald was getting very impatient," former Australia batter Phil Jaques said on ABC. "He wants a response from the batting group and Pat Cummins does as well." Labuschagne was once the top-ranked batter in the world but averages 25.34 across his past 25 Tests [Getty Images] 'Hard to see how Maddinson will survive' Amid all of the doubts, this Australia set-up has a history of backing its established players. When Labuschagne was dropped for a Test against West Indies last year, he was recalled on the back of good domestic form at the start of the Ashes months later. Former openers Usman Khawaja and David Warner were both backed through difficult times. Still, after scores of eight and nought this week, on the back of another duck in Durban, opener Nic Maddinson is now under immense pressure for his place. "It is hard to see how Maddinson will survive to Cape Town," said Gillespie. Dropping the 34-year-old would also bring the attention on to Australia's selectors. Maddinson was recalled to open in this series after a 10-year absence, despite primarily being a middle-order player. "You would have to question the process of what happened in that selection room," Jaques said. "I feel for Nic. He is a good player and good fella but he hasn't had a great couple of Test matches." Maddinson was caught behind off the bowling of Kagiso Rabada in both innings of the second Test [Getty Images] Who else could come in? In being recalled for this series, Maddinson became the ninth different batter to open for Australia since David Warner retired in 2024. Like England in the days after Andrew Strauss, it is a problem proving tricky to solve. If Australia do drop Maddinson, one solution would be to return to a batter who has filled the role before - Matt Renshaw. Renshaw made 190 in the first Test but opened against Bangladesh last month before being moved to number five for this series. Renshaw's promotion would create a space in the middle order. Cameron Green and Josh Inglis are fit again. Either could retake that place. Spin-bowling all-rounder Cooper Connolly is another option. The 23-year-old made his Test debut earlier this year but has only played 12 other first-class matches. All-rounder Beau Webster is another incumbent under pressure, having gone seven innings without a fifty with scores of eight and 18 in Gqeberha. He is yet to make a century in his 12 Tests. "Cooper Connolly will come in, possibly at the expense of Webster," predicted Gillespie. "Labuschagne keeps his spot, Renshaw moves to the top and a batter comes in the middle order - whether Green or Inglis." What about Nathan Lyon? It all leaves Australia scrambling, having looked certain winners of this series when South Africa were 110-6 in their first innings. Their best performer on the final day was Boland, who defended resolutely for more than three hours before being bowled by the impressive South Africa all-rounder Wiaan Mulder after taking five wickets in the first innings. The performance of Boland restarts another debate; how do you get the 37-year-old, pace trio Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Mitchell Starc, plus spinner Nathan Lyon into the same XI? Lyon was the one to miss out here but Cape Town, where the series decider begins on Tuesday, is expected to turn. "Boland has to play," said Gillespie. "He was Australia's best seam bowler. "I don't think it is a lock Lyon could play. You have [left-arm spinner] Matt Kuhnemann here and South Africa basically have all right-handed batsmen. "It is going to be a long selection discussion." From holding all of the cards, Australia are now fielding all of the questions. Sri Lanka make 430 to beat England after Brook's 202

item.title: Sri Lanka make 430 to beat England after Brook's 202
item.description: Only South Africa have scored more to win a one-day international than the 430 scored by Sri Lanka [Getty Images] One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi England 429-4 (50 overs): Brook 202, Root 69, Jacks 66* Sri Lanka 430-8 (49.5 overs): Rathnayake 130, Avishka 97, Shanaka 97 Sri Lanka won by two wickets Scorecard Harry Brook's first double century by an England batter in a one-day international was not enough to prevent his team being stunned by Sri Lanka, who pulled off a remarkable chase of 430 in Rawalpindi. Brook passed Ben Stokes' previous England best score of 182 and posted the fastest ODI double hundred, off 114 balls, in his astonishing 202. In clobbering the 14th double-hundred in a men's one-day international and the 12th highest individual score, Brook lifted England to 429-4 – at halfway the highest total made in a one-day international in Pakistan. But Sri Lanka, who chose to bat second, were not deterred, even when they were reduced to 24-2. They set about completing the second-highest successful chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake made a sublime 130, while Aviksha Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both added 97. With Jofra Archer rested for the tri-series and leg-spinner Adil Rashid left out of this match for tactical reasons, England's bowling was woeful. Sam Curran conceded 103 runs from his nine overs. Up with the required rate throughout their innings, Sri Lanka needed 109 from the final 10 overs and were able to absorb the losses of Rathnayake and Shanaka. Sri Lanka needed eight off the final over, sent down by Josh Tongue, who was pinpoint with his accuracy to bowl Dinuth Wellalage and Eshan Malinga with successive deliveries. But in a sensational finish, Janith Liyanage, the man bowling when Brook reached 200, would not be denied. With six needed from two balls, Liyanage pummelled Tongue's penultimate delivery of the match down the ground for a match-winning maximum, sparking joyous Sri Lankan celebrations. One of the most incredible one-day internationals ever played ended with an aggregate of 847 runs, behind only a match total of 872 when South Africa chased 435 to beat Australia in 2006. The total of 123 boundaries across both innings - 93 fours and 30 sixes - is also a record in ODIs. Relive Sri Lanka's staggering run-chase against England England floored in astonishing ODI How did England lose this game? At halfway, when Brook left the field arm-in-arm with Will Jacks, the thought of Sri Lanka even getting close to their target seemed highly fanciful. Yet, Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis' decision to chase proved inspired, despite the way his team were dismantled by Brook. Ultimately, Sri Lanka put the conditions – and Brook's knock – into context, helped by an England team who wilted under the pressure. They were hampered by the dew, another factor in Sri Lanka's decision to bat second. England made mistakes in the field and their bowlers struggled to grip the ball. Without Archer, they lacked a death bowler. And
item.content:encoded: Only South Africa have scored more to win a one-day international than the 430 scored by Sri Lanka [Getty Images] One-day international tri-series, Rawalpindi England 429-4 (50 overs): Brook 202, Root 69, Jacks 66* Sri Lanka 430-8 (49.5 overs): Rathnayake 130, Avishka 97, Shanaka 97 Sri Lanka won by two wickets Scorecard Harry Brook's first double century by an England batter in a one-day international was not enough to prevent his team being stunned by Sri Lanka, who pulled off a remarkable chase of 430 in Rawalpindi. Brook passed Ben Stokes' previous England best score of 182 and posted the fastest ODI double hundred, off 114 balls, in his astonishing 202. In clobbering the 14th double-hundred in a men's one-day international and the 12th highest individual score, Brook lifted England to 429-4 – at halfway the highest total made in a one-day international in Pakistan. But Sri Lanka, who chose to bat second, were not deterred, even when they were reduced to 24-2. They set about completing the second-highest successful chase in ODI history. Pavan Rathnayake made a sublime 130, while Aviksha Fernando and Dasun Shanaka both added 97. With Jofra Archer rested for the tri-series and leg-spinner Adil Rashid left out of this match for tactical reasons, England's bowling was woeful. Sam Curran conceded 103 runs from his nine overs. Up with the required rate throughout their innings, Sri Lanka needed 109 from the final 10 overs and were able to absorb the losses of Rathnayake and Shanaka. Sri Lanka needed eight off the final over, sent down by Josh Tongue, who was pinpoint with his accuracy to bowl Dinuth Wellalage and Eshan Malinga with successive deliveries. But in a sensational finish, Janith Liyanage, the man bowling when Brook reached 200, would not be denied. With six needed from two balls, Liyanage pummelled Tongue's penultimate delivery of the match down the ground for a match-winning maximum, sparking joyous Sri Lankan celebrations. One of the most incredible one-day internationals ever played ended with an aggregate of 847 runs, behind only a match total of 872 when South Africa chased 435 to beat Australia in 2006. The total of 123 boundaries across both innings - 93 fours and 30 sixes - is also a record in ODIs. Relive Sri Lanka's staggering run-chase against England England floored in astonishing ODI How did England lose this game? At halfway, when Brook left the field arm-in-arm with Will Jacks, the thought of Sri Lanka even getting close to their target seemed highly fanciful. Yet, Sri Lankan captain Kusal Mendis' decision to chase proved inspired, despite the way his team were dismantled by Brook. Ultimately, Sri Lanka put the conditions – and Brook's knock – into context, helped by an England team who wilted under the pressure. They were hampered by the dew, another factor in Sri Lanka's decision to bat second. England made mistakes in the field and their bowlers struggled to grip the ball. Without Archer, they lacked a death bowler. And, with less then a year to go until the World Cup, England showed no composure as the game began to run away from them. For as well as Brook batted, his tactics will come into question. Too much faith was placed in Curran, whose 103-2 are the most expensive figures returned by an England bowler in an ODI. Gus Atkinson opened the bowling and sent down just seven overs of his allotted 10 and Tongue, who almost rescued the game, was only into his ninth. This tri-series is designed to replicate the tournament conditions England will face at the World Cup in southern Africa. Two games in they are without a win and facing the prospect of needing to beat Pakistan in Lahore on Sunday to stay in the competition. Brook record not enough Brook's previous highest score in ODIs was 136 not out, also against Sri Lanka [Getty Images] Brook has become the first man in ODI history to make a double hundred and end up on the losing side. His strokeplay was irresistible. In a 116-ball stay, he mixed innovation with brutal power and deft touches. He scored all around the ground, clearing the ropes for 10 sixes and adding 21 fours. A feature of Brook's knock was his measured acceleration. The 27-year-old had only 13 runs from the first 24 deliveries he faced, then upped the pace to reach 50 from 42 balls. His century, his fourth in ODIs, was completed in 75 balls. It was upon reaching three figures that Brook really cut loose. He went from 100 to 200 in only 39 balls. As England added 156 in the final 10 overs, Brook passed Stokes' record with a six whipped over the leg side off a full toss bowled by left-arm seamer Dilshan Madushanka. Whether he was aware of the milestone or not, Brook did not acknowledge his achievement and, in the same over, was dropped at mid-off on 185. Brook began the final over, delivered by seamer Liyanage, on 186. He clobbered the first ball over the covers for six, then scampered back for two unlikely twos. Fittingly, the double hundred was reached with a paddled-sweep, then he was caught at third man off the final ball of the innings. Somehow, it was not enough. Liyanage had the final say. 'They played an absolute blinder' England captain Harry Brook: "Heart-breaking. It's very disappointing that we haven't been able to defend 430 but that's life, that's cricket. "You don't see many teams chase down 430 and hats off to Sri Lanka, they've played exceptionally well. We couldn't execute our skills enough with the ball and they've just played an absolute blinder there. "It's extremely disappointing but we know where we went wrong. We'll have a good chat about it now and over the next couple of days. We've got a good opportunity in the next couple of games to really try and get to that final in Lahore." Ex-England bowler Steven Finn on Test Match Special: "I think this might make England question the balance of their team. I think it has been exacerbated with the top order scoring all the runs. "But we've still had in the hutch today Sam Curran, Jordan Cox, Jamie Overton, Liam Dawson - that's almost too much batting for an ODI team." England & Sri Lanka tri-series in Pakistan 2026 - schedule What next for Australia after chastening defeat by South Africa?

item.title: Renault Enters Deal to Sell Alpine Racing’s Viry-Chatillon Base That Made F1 Engines
item.description: Groupe Renault and Dumarey Group have agreed for the latter to acquire Alpine Racing SAS – the Viry-Chatillon base. The Viry base made headlines when the employees resisted Groupe Renault’s decision to end the F1 powertrain business after decades of production, ahead of the 2026 season, when Alpine took the customer route with Mercedes-Benz. After the F1 work ended at the site, the Viry base produced powertrains for Alpine ’s A524 machinery to compete in the FIA World Endurance Championship. However, the future looked uncertain after the decision to discontinue the WEC program after the 2026 season. Dumeray Steps in To Buy Alpine Racing Base Alpine F1 pair at Turn 1 | Photo Credit: Alpine F1 Team Amid speculation about Signatech taking over, there is official confirmation that the Viry base will be acquired by Belgian powertrain specialists Dumarey Group. It has snapped up both the ‘tangible and intangible assets required to operate the site’. Dumarey is looking to expand its expertise in motorsport, and the opportunity came at the right time. It is unclear if it will continue the WEC programme. It is also not certain if there is any change in the F1 side of things as things stand. But Dumarey has highlighted that it will strengthen the core business of Alpine Racing SAS’s teams to create opportunities to leverage the F1 engine expertise for racing teams in the future. The proposed acquisition was presented at a Works Council meeting of Alpine Racing SAS on October 22, 2026. It will go through the required regulatory and legal steps before a full transfer. After that, the company will run under the Dumarey Group brand, ownership and management. The move is expected to save the jobs of many employees. Dumarey Group Impressed By the Facility And Its Capabilities “Motorsport has always been at the heart of the activities of Alpine Tech’s Viry-Chatillon site,” said the press note. “This center of excellence benefits from more than four decades of Formula 1 development experience, as well as recognized expertise in hybrid and electric propulsion systems, simulation, software and testing. “For its part, Dumarey Group is seeking to diversify its activities into motorsport and intends to strengthen and further expand its engineering capabilities by adding world-class expertise in high-performance powertrain development, electrification and advanced testing technologies. “This combination would represent a strong strategic fit with Dumarey’s ambition to accelerate innovation across the automotive, aerospace and industrial sectors.” The Belgian company sees big potential, not just of the Viry base but also the people, to expand the company’s horizon. “The Viry-Châtillon site has built a strong reputation for advanced engineering and innovation,” said Guido Dumarey, Chairman and Founder of Dumarey Group. “We see considerable potential in combining its highly skilled teams and technical capabilities with Dumarey’s entrepreneurial culture and diversified indu

The Viry base made headlines when the employees resisted Groupe Renault’s decision to end the F1 powertrain business after decades of production, ahead of the 2026 season, when Alpine took the customer route with Mercedes-Benz. After the F1 work ended at the site, the Viry base produced powertrains for Alpine ’s A524 machinery to compete in the FIA World Endurance Championship. However, the future looked uncertain after the decision to discontinue the WEC program after the 2026 season. Dumeray Steps in To Buy Alpine Racing Base Alpine F1 pair at Turn 1 | Photo Credit: Alpine F1 Team Amid speculation about Signatech taking over, there is official confirmation that the Viry base will be acquired by Belgian powertrain specialists Dumarey Group. It has snapped up both the ‘tangible and intangible assets required to operate the site’. Dumarey is looking to expand its expertise in motorsport, and the opportunity came at the right time. It is unclear if it will continue the WEC programme. It is also not certain if there is any change in the F1 side of things as things stand. But Dumarey has highlighted that it will strengthen the core business of Alpine Racing SAS’s teams to create opportunities to leverage the F1 engine expertise for racing teams in the future. The proposed acquisition was presented at a Works Council meeting of Alpine Racing SAS on October 22, 2026. It will go through the required regulatory and legal steps before a full transfer. After that, the company will run under the Dumarey Group brand, ownership and management. The move is expected to save the jobs of many employees. Dumarey Group Impressed By the Facility And Its Capabilities “Motorsport has always been at the heart of the activities of Alpine Tech’s Viry-Chatillon site,” said the press note. “This center of excellence benefits from more than four decades of Formula 1 development experience, as well as recognized expertise in hybrid and electric propulsion systems, simulation, software and testing. “For its part, Dumarey Group is seeking to diversify its activities into motorsport and intends to strengthen and further expand its engineering capabilities by adding world-class expertise in high-performance powertrain development, electrification and advanced testing technologies. “This combination would represent a strong strategic fit with Dumarey’s ambition to accelerate innovation across the automotive, aerospace and industrial sectors.” The Belgian company sees big potential, not just of the Viry base but also the people, to expand the company’s horizon. “The Viry-Châtillon site has built a strong reputation for advanced engineering and innovation,” said Guido Dumarey, Chairman and Founder of Dumarey Group. “We see considerable potential in combining its highly skilled teams and technical capabilities with Dumarey’s entrepreneurial culture and diversified industrial footprint. Alpine Pleased to See its Tech Flourishing “Our ambition is to preserve and further develop this exceptional engineering expertise while creating new opportunities for growth.” At the same time, Alpine is pleased that its technology has found market support and that the deal is progressing well to secure the jobs and further develop the expertise. “This transaction represents a strong and coherent opportunity to secure and further develop the expertise of the Viry-Châtillon site,” said Axel Plasse, VP Alpine Tech. “It opens up new prospects for employees and for the engineering business. This development is a recognition of the site’s longstanding motorsport expertise, particularly in Formula 1.” Adobe Partners with Alpine F1 Team In other news, global technology leader Adobe has entered into a deal with Alpine F1 Team as its Official AI Fan Experience Partner. It aims to use its technology, creativity and productivity to enhance the consumer and fan experience. It is a first for the American company to enter Formula 1. The partnership will see the use of Adobe GenStudio, Adobe Experience Platform, Adobe Brand Visibility and Adobe Express. “Formula One has become so much more than what happens on the track, becoming a global sports phenomenon where engineering excellence, innovation, sustainability and cultural connection meet,” said Marissa Dacay, global vice president of enterprise marketing, Adobe. “Our partnership with BWT Alpine Formula One Team showcases how Adobe’s AI technology is powering new ways to drive fan engagement around the world, creating more personalized connections and providing fans different ways to share their passion for the sport.” Alpine is looking to enhance the experience for its fans worldwide. “We are entering an incredibly exciting new era for BWT Alpine Formula One Team, and creativity and personalisation will be at the heart of how we express our ambitions, our identity, and our connection with audiences and fans worldwide. “Adobe is an incredible partner for this journey, giving us the tools to bring our vision to life in new and unexpected ways. Together we have an opportunity to create experiences that extend far beyond the racetrack,” said Guy Martin, global marketing director, Alpine.

item.title: President Trump calls LeBron James ‘Total disgrace’
item.description: President Donald Trump has taken aim at NBA superstar LeBron James after video surfaced showing the Philadelphia 76ers forward appearing to practice his golf swing and shooting motion during the national anthem. Trump: "While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE. LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for! President DONALD J. TRUMP" — Aaron Rupar (@atrupar) October 22, 2026 This “incident2 occured before Tuesday’s season opener against the New York Knicks. Trump called James a “TOTAL DISGRACE” and demanded an apology from the 41-year-old star. MORE: Nikola Jokic chasing NBA history in Nuggets season opener Trump blasts LeBron James over national anthem behavior President Donald Trump speaks Wednesday evening, Oct. 21, 2020, as he held a rally outside under the stars at the Gastonia Municipal Airport on Gaston Day School Road. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Trump addressed the controversy Thursday in a post on Truth Social, sharing a video of James standing alongside his 76ers teammates as the national anthem played at Madison Square Garden. “While listening to our National Anthem, LeBron James disrespects our Country! I said right from the beginning that he’s no good, a TOTAL DISGRACE,” Trump wrote. Trump went further by saying James should apologize to American military veterans and those who died defending the country. “LeBron James should apologize to all of those Great American Warriors and Heroes who died for the American Flag, and all that our Country stands for!” Trump added. LeBron James seen messing around during the national anthem. https://t.co/fzt4kHzoIn — Leading Report (@LeadingReport) October 22, 2026 The video shows James moving his arms and appearing to go through a golf-swing motion before also mimicking his basketball shooting form. The footage quickly spread across social media, generating criticism from fans who viewed the behavior as inappropriate during the anthem. However, the footage itself does not establish what James intended by the movements, and there has been no indication that he was making a political statement or deliberately protesting the anthem. James also received a hostile reception from Knicks fans throughout the night. The crowd repeatedly chanted “We don’t want you!” at the former Lakers star, referencing his previous interest in potentially joining New York during free agency.
