item.title: Charles Barkley roasts Shaq over Kash Patel connection
item.description: Credit: ESPN, U.S. government Less than an hour into Inside the NBA coverage of the 2026-27 season, the always-honest Charles Barkley said something that caught host Ernie Johnson off guard. During the NBA Tip-Off pregame show ahead of Wednesday night’s ESPN NBA doubleheader, Barkley mentioned that Shaquille O’Neal knows FBI Director Kash Patel. The way Barkley delivered the point had everyone on the crew, including O’Neal, laughing. “Hey, Kenny. Should we be standing this close to Shaq?” Barkley asked. “Why is that?” Kenny Smith responded. “He’s been hanging out with Kash Patel,” Barkley explained. “That’s dangerous.” “Oh!! Oh! item.title: High School Football: See our staff picks for Week 9 in the High Desert
item.description: The race atop our weekly High Desert football picks tightened up a little last week. Todd Hadler and HD Football Report both turned in perfect 9-0 records, while Jose Quintero went 8-1 to maintain his lead in the season-long standings. Quintero’s lone miss came in one of the closest games of the week. He took Serrano over Hesperia, but the Scorpions escaped with a 28-27 victory after stopping a two-point conversion attempt in the final minute. Quintero is now 82-16 overall, with Hadler just two games back at 80-18. HD Football Report’s perfect week moved it to 75-23, while James Quigg went 8-1 to improve to 72-26. Jason Reed finished 7-2 and now sits at 67-31. With the regular season winding down and the standings still within reach, every pick is starting to matter a little more. Here’s where everyone stands and who we’re taking in Week 9. Each week we will keep a running tab of our leaderboard throughout the season, up until there are no local teams left vying for a CIF-Southern Section title in the playoffs. Which picks did we get right, or wrong? Feel free to chime in on social media on Instagram @760Varsity, or on X @J0seQuintero. This article originally appeared on Victorville Daily Press: High School Football: See our staff picks for Week 9 in the High Desert

item.title: ‘She needed to get better’: Nick Wright weighs in on Angel Reese
item.description: Oct 19, 2026; San Francisco, California, USA; Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) drives to the basket against Golden State Valkyries center Kiah Stokes (41) in the fourth quarter of game two of the 2026 WNBA Finals at Chase Center. Mandatory Credit: David Gonzales-Imagn Images Atlanta Dream star Angel Reese is coming off a “phenomenal” season as she averaged 16 points, 12 rebounds, and nearly 2 steals per game for the 2026 season. The Dream are currently in the WNBA Finals against the Golden State Valkyries, and Reese continues to contribute to the stat sheet well into the postseason. On his What’s Wright? with Nick Wright podcast, Fox Sports’ Nick Wright discussed Reese’s drastic improvements on the court despite public scrutiny. “I understand because some folks are either fools or charlatans or bad actors,” Wright said . “They can’t hear a white commentator talk about a Black WNBA player without calling it virtue signaling, some type of bullsh*t, or trying to make Caitlin Clark a part of this story. “I’m just calling it as I see it: if Angel Reese was going to have her status as a player stay at the level of her status as a celebrity, she needed to get better. It felt like her game had stagnated, if not dipped.” The Chicago Sky traded Reese before the season began after she spent two years with the organization. At the start of the WNBA season, expectations were high for the forward as a new team and system would show her true talent with the Dream’s loaded roster. Reese has been consistently criticized since her emergence in the league for her fierce, confident, and unapologetic attitude. Off the court, she quickly rose to celebrity status as an influencer in fashion, media, and pop culture, walking in fashion shows and hosting her own Unapologetically Angel podcast. Wright doubted her ability to balance her lifestyle with her career, but after this year, he believes Reese is just a step behind 2026 MVP A’ja Wilson. “This year that changed considerably; she’s been phenomenal,” Wright added. “Angel Reese’s performance these playoffs, as she might have her team on the doorstep of a championship, gives her the opportunity to be right alongside, I’ll call it a step behind, A’ja Wilson as the top player in the sport.” Reese and the Dream took a 2-1 lead in the 2026 WNBA Finals with a 97-71 win in Game 3 on Wednesday, and they can move within one win of a championship in Game 4 on Saturday in Atlanta. The post ‘She needed to get better’: Nick Wright weighs in on Angel Reese appeared first on The Comeback: Today’s Top Sports Stories & Reactions .

item.title: The reason Jack Draper is currently playing tennis in Brazil with Joao Fonseca
item.description: Jack Draper’s absence from the ATP Tour of late has been an expected one, given all the fitness troubles he’s suffered in recent years. And, given the specific nature of his current injury, the only real antidote is rest. For a professional athlete, that is nearly impossible to do, and tennis is arguably even worse. With no security and a ranking system that benefits the ever-present, Jack Draper has suffered both financially and in terms of his stature: the Brit currently sits outside the world’s top 150. However, it seems that whatever recovery plan he and his team agreed on has reached its next step, with reports now emerging that he is back on court. Jack Draper spotted training in Rio, Brazil It’s not just reports that have confirmed Draper’s return to on-court action, with photos and videos also surfacing. The 24-year-old has been pictured training in Rio, Brazil, at the same country club where Joao Fonseca started playing tennis. Imagens de Jack Draper no Country Club Ipanema no Rio de Janeiro, Brasil ❤️ pic.twitter.com/Smst2DHXaI — AhhSabrina (@AhhhSabrina) October 21, 2026 In fact, the Brazilian youngster is apparently there now as well, with one update claiming his plan is to ‘get in shape physically and tennis-wise for next year.’ They added: “He also wants to build up his tolerance to high temperatures.” Fonseca has also ended his season early , as part of a growing list of players struck down by injury. He was seen at the same club on Tuesday, although pictures of him and Draper together remain unreleased. Jack Draper’s curious decision to play on clay courts What is particularly interesting about this decision is not the timing of his return, but where he has chosen to return. After all, opting to return to practice on clay courts seems odd with the Australian Open likely his ultimate target after taking so long off. Photo by Charlie Crowhurst/Getty Images for LTA Even if he were to miss that first Grand Slam of the year, the clay-court season does not start until April, assuming he does play any events during the Golden Swing in Brazil and Argentina, across February. Naturally, the warm weather seems to be his focus, but that could have been achieved on any surface. The clay must have been a conscious choice, and a curious one at that.

item.title: Bears vs. Patriots Predictions: Can Caleb Williams replicate OPOW performance in short week?
item.description: Brett Davis-Imagn Images I’ve got a take for you: Bears nickel back Kyler Gordon should’ve won NFC Defensive Player of the Week for Week 6. It’s almost shocking he didn’t. He played 17 defensive snaps, rushed on 10 of ‘em and came away with three sacks and two forced fumbles. Hey, at least Caleb Williams took home the NFC Offensive Player of the Week honors. He’s the second Bears QB to ever win the award twice, joining good ol’ Jay Cutler. Let’s turn the page and dive into Week 7. WEEK 7 PREDICTIONS Adam Hoge (4-2) | Bears 28, Patriots 27 The Bears have only played in one close game this season — Week 2 against the Vikings — and Caleb Williams wasn’t able to finish the game. This one feels like it will come down to the wire, and this time the Bears should have Iceman in there to close. Adam Jahns (4-2) | Bears 27, Patriots 23 This is a matchup of two very good teams . The numbers show that on both sides of the ball. But give me Caleb Williams over Drake Maye — and I think everyone will see why on Thursday Night Football. But let’s hope this is the start of something fun to cover and watch in the future, too. They’re friends who can grow into rivals. It’s easy to see both quarterbacks becoming the new, young faces of the NFL. Mark Carman (2-4) | Bears 27, Patriots 17 Banged-up New England offensive line spells trouble for the Patriots. Bears score early and Soldier Field is rocking with 5-2 excitement. Patrick Norton (3-3) | Bears 30, Patriots 22 I’ve got two words for you: Caleb Williams and Drake Maye — must-see TV. I promise you that’ll make sense to a couple of people … to which I say: worth it. Williams having his full offensive line — including right guard Jonah Jackson — is a big deal. Maye, meanwhile, does not have his full group. The last time we saw him perform with an inferior offensive line, the results weren’t exactly ideal (SEE: Super Bowl LX). Greg Braggs Jr. (3-3) | Bears 34, Patriots 20 This feels like a buzzsaw game for the Patriots. Caleb Williams is riding high after his comeback in Atlanta. The Patriots offensive line is heavily banged up. Soldier Field will be rocking. Ticket prices have risen to NFC Championship-level numbers. Not sure New England is ready for what they are about to walk into. Joey Christopoulos (3-3) | Bears 24, Patriots 17 It’s gonna be tight, but Ben Johnson and Caleb Williams are ready for a tight win against a formidable NFL opponent. I’m looking for a big shot play down the field as the separator. Stephen Nicholas (3-3) | Bears 27, Patriots 24 Ben Johnson’s team protects home turf where he has an 8-3 record as Bears head coach. I don’t think Caleb utilizes his legs very much after seeing the Patriots hold Josh Allen to just four yards rushing in their matchup with the Bills. Luther Burden is the beneficiary as Ben uses pre-snap motions to get Christian Gonzalez away from his top targets. item.title: Michael Mosiman joins Quad Lock Honda for 2027 SuperMotocross
item.description: Michael Mosiman will race for the Quadlock Honda Racing team in all three SuperMotocross World Championship series in the 250 division in 2027, joining Cameron McAdoo who also announced his move to the team in early October. Debuting in 2017 with four rounds of the Pro Motocross series, Mosiman brings a decade of experience to the team. His first Supercross top-five finish came in 2019 with a fourth-place result in Seattle. He won his first, and so far only, SuperMotocross race in 2022 in San Diego. Nate Thrasher joins Pro Circuit Kawasaki for 2027 Nate Thrasher will become the fifth rider in the Monster Energy Pro Circuit Kawasaki team, joining SMX champion Levi Kitchen and others. Dan Beaver , "I’ve watched this team grow and build momentum over the years," Mosiman said in a news release. "They’ve won races in the 250 class and achieved podiums in the 450 class. They seem to have their riders' backs and do everything in their power to help them achieve their goals. "I want to reach my potential and see how good I can become as an athlete. I pushed to be a part of this program because I believe this is a place where I can progress my skills, develop the motorcycle and put myself in a position to fight for championships. Kevin Windham’s involvement was a big part of that decision, and I’m excited about what we can accomplish together." The team will field four 250 bikes in 2027. In addition to McAdoo, Brodie Connelly and Alex Larwood on the small bike. Christian Craig competes on the 450 with Charli Cannon in the Women's Pro Motocross (WMX) series. "Michael is one of the most talented riders in the class," said Yarrive Konsky, team owner. "His race win, championship result and career performances demonstrate what he can do, he has claimed two podiums this year and many top fives. We’re building a program around winning, not simply participating. American Honda has stepped up its support, Kevin is committed to helping us develop the riders and the team, and we’re putting the right resources in place. "Michael has the speed and experience. Our job is to give him the environment, equipment and support to convert that potential into consistent results. We believe he can fight for championships, and that’s exactly what we’re working towards."

item.title: Dan Miller Announces When He Will Return to Lions Radio Booth
item.description: The Detroit Lions will have a familiar voice back in the broadcast booth Sunday, as longtime radio play-by-play announcer Dan Miller announced Thursday that he plans to return for Detroit’s NFC North showdown against the Green Bay Packers. Miller has been away from the team following the heartbreaking passing of his wife, Cindy, on October 10 after a battle with cancer. On Thursday, he shared an emotional message thanking the Detroit community for its overwhelming support. The WJR-AM broadcast team of Dan Miller (foreground) and spotter Joe Abramson on Sunday, September 20, 2020 call the action of the Detroit Lions game against the Green Bay Packers. The broadcast was done at Ford Field though the team was playing at Lambeau Field. Lions Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Dan Miller Announces Return, Thanks Lions Fans In a message shared on his X account , Miller expressed appreciation for the donations and kindness his family has received. “Hello again. Looking forward to getting back to work this weekend. My family continues to heal and I want to again thank you for your role in that. The support has been incredible. Over 500 donations for more than 43k to LMCancer.org.” Miller also recognized Jeremy Reisman and the Pride of Detroit community for helping organize the fundraising effort. He praised Justin Rogers and the Detroit Football Network for raising another $10,000 for Metro Detroit Animals, an organization close to his and Cindy’s hearts. Thanks to Jeremy and @PrideOfDetroit for getting that going. That money will hopefully help extend lives as we learn more about the disease. @Justin_Rogers and his Detroit Football Network raised 10k for @MetroDetAnimals , a group Cindy & I love and a passion JRog & I Share. — Dan Miller (@DanMillerFox2) October 22, 2026 The generosity has been remarkable, with Lions fans turning their support for Miller into contributions that could help others battling devastating diseases. Lions Family Continues to Rally Around Miller Miller missed Detroit’s October 11 victory over the Arizona Cardinals, with Jason Benetti stepping in alongside Lomas Brown for the radio broadcast. As we previously reported , head coach Dan Campbell dedicated the game ball to Miller and his family following the Lions’ 45-21 victory. Quarterback Jared Goff also delivered an emotional message, emphasizing how much Miller means to the organization and its players. Miller previously thanked the Detroit community during an appearance on FOX 2, describing how meaningful the support had been as his family navigated its loss. The donations made in Cindy’s memory will support efforts related to leptomeningeal cancer, a devastating disease that remains difficult to treat. Fans interested in contributing can learn more through the Leptomeningeal Cancer Foundation , while additional details about the community’s initial fundraising effort were shared in earlier coverage of the remarkable response . Miller previously thanked the Detroit community during an appearance on FOX 2, describing how meaningful the support had been as his family navigated its loss. The donations made in Cindy’s memory will support efforts related to leptomeningeal cancer, a devastating disease that remains difficult to treat. Fans interested in contributing can learn more through the Leptomeningeal Cancer Foundation , while additional details about the community’s initial fundraising effort were shared in earlier coverage of the remarkable response . For more than two decades, Miller’s voice has accompanied some of the most unforgettable moments in Lions history. His expected return Sunday will undoubtedly be a meaningful moment for him, his family, and the thousands of Detroit fans who have supported him through an incredibly difficult time. Welcome back, Dan. The Lions family is glad to have you back.

item.title: Toya Jones, a former Texas A&M football player and Texas high school track legend, dead at 49
item.description: Texas A&M's Toya Jones (5) and Dat Nguyen (left) celebrate after Jones recovered a fumble during a Missouri punt return in the fourth quarter Saturday, Nov. 14, 1998, in College Station. The fumble recovery led Texas A&M to their game-winning field goal, giving them a 17-14 win over Missouri. (DAVID J. PHILLIP/AP) Former Texas A&M football and track star Toya Jones died Thursday. The 49-year-old suffered a heart attack last weekend and was placed in hospice care Wednesday. With Jones, who played defensive back and ran track at Texas A&M from 1995-98, in hospice care, friends and family gathered around him this week to say goodbye. "Today is a very difficult day for me and so many others. I have to say goodbye to one of my closest friends for more than 20 years," Randy Keisler, a former Major League Baseball pitcher and close friend of Jones, wrote on Facebook on Thursday . "Toya, you were the funniest guy I've ever known and your personality was one of a kind. Your positive outlook on life, your smile, sense of humor and always making anyone around you laugh and feel better just being with you was an awesome gift that you possessed. I could be down and out and you would make me laugh or somehow just feel better with your infectious smile and sense of humor. I love you brother and it's a shame that the world is losing you today." On the football field, Jones is best known for his tackle that saved the Aggies' Big 12 championship his senior year. In the 1998 Big 12 title game, Texas A&M came roaring back from 15 points down in the fourth quarter against undefeated Kansas State, but nearly suffered a heartbreaking loss when the Wildcats' Michael Bishop completed a 54-yard Hail Mary to Everett Burnett as time expired in regulation, but Jones was there to make the tackle at the 1-yard line. The Aggies went on to win in double overtime and claim what still stands as their last conference championship. "What a great guy. This is so sad," R.C. Slocum, who recruited and coached Jones, wrote on Facebook . "He was a special athlete and person. God rest his soul." Jones spent time in training camp with the San Francisco 49ers in 1999, Denver Broncos in 2000 and Houston Texans in 2002, but never appeared in an NFL regular season game. He played for the XFL's Birmingham Thunderbolts in 2001 and spent two seasons in the Canadian Football League with the British Columbia Lions. Texans free safety Toya Jones gets a cooldown from a trainer during Thursday afternoon's training camp at the team's training facility in Houston. 7/25/2002 Karl Stolleis/Houston Chronicle (Karl Stolleis/Houston Chronicle) Jones was an even bigger star on the track where he still stands as one of the best high school track athletes in state history. At Refugio High School, Jones, who was inducted into the Texas Track & Field Hall of Fame in 2020 , won a record 17 medals in his career at the state meet - including 13 golds - and led his team to three state championships. He won 147 points

Texans free safety Toya Jones gets a cooldown from a trainer during Thursday afternoon's training camp at the team's training facility in Houston. 7/25/2002 Karl Stolleis/Houston Chronicle (Karl Stolleis/Houston Chronicle) Jones was an even bigger star on the track where he still stands as one of the best high school track athletes in state history. At Refugio High School, Jones, who was inducted into the Texas Track & Field Hall of Fame in 2020 , won a record 17 medals in his career at the state meet - including 13 golds - and led his team to three state championships. He's still one of only two boys to ever win five gold medals at the Texas state meet. Jones was a sprinter and a long jumper at Texas A&M and ran the second leg on the Aggies' 1997 NCAA champion 400-meter relay team, which went undefeated that season with wins at the Texas Relays, Penn Relays and the Big 12 Championships, as well as the NCAAs. Track and field star Toya Jones at Refugio High School on May 10, 1995. When he was done with sports, Jones had a successful career in sales in the Houston area. He worked at Houston's Sagis Diagnostics, then founded Sagis Transport in Sugar Land in 2017. The company was honored by Texas A&M's McFerrin Center for Entrepreneurship in 2023 and 2024 as one of the Aggie 100 , which honors the top 100 business owned or operated by Texas A&M graduates. item.title: Why Brandon Woodruff isn’t a lock for Brewers’ World Series roster
item.description: Kevin Sousa-Imagn Images Why Brandon Woodruff isn’t a lock for Brewers’ World Series roster appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . In recent weeks, it seems as if Brandon Woodruff has been trending toward a return from injury in the World Series. The Milwaukee Brewers pitcher is recovering from a shoulder injury. Woodruff is hoping to earn a spot on the roster of course. However, MLB insider Ken Rosenthal recently explained a specific World Series rule that suggests this is going to be a tougher decision for Milwaukee than it may have initially seemed. “He has worked his way back, turned out he healed quickly enough so he didn’t need surgery. And he went on a throwing progression and suddenly now, after throwing to live hitters Tuesday, is a guy at least they’re thinking about for the (World Series) roster,” Rosenthal said on Foul Territory. “Now, you ask about the rule… here’s the problem. The way the rules work, if an injured player is replaced for an injury he suffers during the particular series… or something that just comes up, he can be replaced. If it is a situation where the injury is chronic or recurring, well then you have a situation where in the rules it says, ‘No, you cannot replace the player.'” Rosenthal further explained that if Woodruff hurt his shoulder again during a World Series appearance, he may not be able to be replaced since it’s an injury he’s dealt with for months now. It’s something the Brewers will have to think about before placing him on the roster. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Woodruff has pitched in Milwaukee since 2017. The two-time All-Star has seen the highs and lows of the franchise over the years. One could argue he deserves the roster spot despite the rule. With that being said, the Brewers would be placed in a difficult position if Woodruff were to reaggravate his injury early in the series. That could potentially leave them with an injured player occupying a valuable roster spot. This will be a storyline to follow as the Brewers prepare to officially announce their World Series roster soon. Game 1 of the 2026 Fall Classic between the Brewers and Tampa Bay Rays is scheduled for 8 PM ET on Friday night. Related: World Series injuries: Brewers, Rays could be without these key players in Fall Classic Related: This Jacob Misiorowski-Drew Rasmussen World Series comparison will catch Brewers, Rays fans’ attention

item.title: Ron Duguay, Former NHL Player and Sarah Palin’s Boyfriend, Dies at 69
item.description: Ron Duguay attends the 2017 Tony Awards at Radio City Music Hall on June 11, 2017 in New York City. (Credit: Sylvain Gaboury/Patrick McMullan via Getty Images) Retired New York Rangers star Ron Duguay died Thursday at the age of 69. His death was confirmed by his partner and former Alaska Governor Sarah Palin . “It’s with a shattered heart, but also deep peace knowing Ron is with Jesus now,” Palin wrote on Instagram. “He fought so hard. Love never ends.” A celebration of life for Duguay will be announced “at a later date,” Palin wrote. The political commentator and former 2008 Republican vice presidential candidate previously shared just days ago a photo on Instagram of herself holding Duguay’s hand in a hospital bed. She wrote at the time that prayers would be “so appreciated.” The former NHL star’s death comes over a year after he was diagnosed with stage 4 colon cancer. In February, his daughters Shay Thomas and Amber Stavros created a GoFundMe for the NHL legend, writing, “We’ve seen firsthand the weight this battle has placed on him, both physically and financially.” “Our dad has never been someone who asks for help,” Thomas wrote. “Especially when it comes to money. He has always tried to handle everything on his own and didn’t want to burden anyone else with what he’s going through. But after many conversations as a family, we decided to create this fundraiser for him.” That same month, Duguay told Page Six his cancer had originated in his colon and spread to his appendix and gallbladder. He addressed the GoFundMe, admitting, “I find it extremely hard asking for funds for all these costs I’m going through. Normally, I’m helping others.” The former NHL star added that cancer not only “sucks the life out of you” but is also “so freaking costly.” Born in Ontario, Canada, Duguay played in the NHL for 12 seasons from 1977 through 1988. Throughout that time, he was a member of the Rangers, Detroit Red Wings, Los Angeles Kings and Pittsburgh Penguins. Duguay and Palin’s relationship was first reported and confirmed in 2022. Before he began dating the former Alaska governor, Duguay was married two times. He first married model Robin Bobo in December 1983. They share two daughters. Following their divorce, he married model Kim Alexis in 1993 and stayed with her until their divorce in 2016. They share a 32-year-old son. The Rangers recognized his death with a team statement Thursday. “The New York Rangers organization mourns the loss of Ron Duguay, one of the most popular players in franchise history,” the team said Thursday. “Ron’s signature skating style – with his hair flowing as he moved down the ice – captivated The Garden Faithful, and his skill, tenacity, and charisma earned him the admiration of all New Yorkers. We join the hockey community in sending our condolences to Ron’s friends, family and loved ones during this difficult time.” The post Ron Duguay, Former NHL Player and Sarah Palin’s Boyfriend, Dies at 69 appeared first on TheWrap .

item.title: Danica Patrick praises Trump after rally: 'He is so easy to talk to'
item.description: Danica Patrick sang President Donald Trump's praises, saying he is "so easy to talk to" after traveling with him to a recent political rally. The former NASCAR and IndyCar driver took to Instagram on Oct. 21 to share photos of herself with Trump, including one traveling in his motorcade and others from Air Force One. While urging fans to vote in the midterm elections, Patrick lauded the president as "a great story teller … funny and obviously interesting." "I wish you could all have just 5 minutes with @potus! He is so easy to talk to and SO fun to listen to!" she wrote. Patrick, who retired from racing in 2018, was in the audience as Trump spoke at a rally in Park City, Kansas, for Sen. Roger Marshall on Oct. 19. Patrick, 44, has been a vocal Trump supporter since his 2024 run. She previously revealed on Instagram that she voted for the first time in that year's race. Danica Patrick praises Trump's 'intelligence, leadership' Patrick wrote in her lengthy Instagram post that Trump "is also very curious what your opinion is pertaining to any topic." "There will never be another Donald J. Trump! He not only loves his country deeply but delivers intelligence, leadership, entertainment and humor all day long," she added. Two years ago, Patrick revealed that she voted for the first time when casting her ballot for Trump in the 2024 presidential election. "I made a rule for myself that if I didn’t vote I could not have an opinion about the outcome, because I didn’t earn that right. Not this time," she wrote on Instagram at the time. Trump calls Danica Patrick 'beautiful and unbelievably brave' Trump called Patrick a "star" while he was speaking on stage at the Park City rally. "She's beautiful and unbelievably brave," he said. "One of the greatest race car drivers, and she happened to do it in a little bit of a man's sport, I would say, just slightly, but she was great and just highly competitive." This isn't the first time Trump has mentioned Patrick while she was in the audience. At a Turning Point USA event in April, Trump said: "I love Danica. I love her hair. I always liked her hair, like the little widow's peak." Melina Khan is a national trending reporter for USA TODAY. Keep up with her on X @melinakh and Instagram @bymelinakhan . This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Danica Patrick praises Trump after rally: 'He is so easy to talk to'

item.title: Penn State Commits in Action: 2028 QB Shines
item.description: STATE COLLEGE, PENNSYLVANIA - SEPTEMBER 19: Associate head coach Terry Smith of the Penn State Nittany Lions looks on during the alma mater after the game against the Buffalo Bulls at Beaver Stadium on September 19, 2026 in State College, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Isaiah Vazquez/Getty Images) | Getty Images Things have gone from bad to worse for Matt Campbell and Penn State, both on the field and on the recruiting trail. The Nittany Lions recently lost the commitment of three-star Massachusetts quarterback Will Wood , who flipped to Boston College this week. This leaves Campbell without a quarterback in his 2027 class. Lucky for Penn State, 2028 quarterback James Armstrong is having a fruitful junior year. Hopewell (Pa.) has now won five in a row, including a 60-0 victory, thanks to its three-star QB. Armstrong finished the most recent victory with 243 passing yards and four touchdowns, also adding 80 yards on the ground. The game ended in a mercy rule. Senior running back Chukwuma Odoh scores from 11-yards out. Back-to-back scoring drives going back to the first half for Paramus Catholic. 14-7, Paladins with their first lead of the day. 9:28 left in 3rd. pic.twitter.com/lXxLSOA9eR — Dhani Joseph (@TheDhaniJoseph) October 10, 2026 Class of 2027 cornerback Kei’Shjuan Telfair is continuing to have two-way success during his senior season at Euclid (Oh.). The four-star has logged multiple three-touchdown performances this season, including a recent win over Cleveland Heights, where he took three of his four receptions to the house. The only catch he didn’t score on was a sure interception that he ripped from the defender’s hands. Pretty ridiculous. pic.twitter.com/32OO8ogrKn — Kei’shjuan Telfair (@Ke1Telfair) October 12, 2026 4 receptions 3tds WENT FED pic.twitter.com/rlJuSUePxt — Kei’shjuan Telfair (@Ke1Telfair) October 10, 2026 It’s too early to tell if Telfair can truly be a two-way threat at Penn State, but he’s surely getting plenty of reps on the offensive side of the ball in high school. item.title: Carter Mazur's role grows as he adjusts to NHL life with Red Wings
item.description: VANCOUVER, Canada — Carter Mazur has been waiting for this opportunity his whole life, and now he's in it. Mazur, 24, made the Red Wings' roster out of training camp, and he's getting into the lineup. Not consistently, as he's played four of the first nine games, but he's playing, contributing, and getting used to the NHL game. Now, it's just a matter of making the most of the opportunities and staying in the lineup. "I'm feeling pretty good," Mazur said of how he's adapting to the NHL. "Again, it's a hard league to play in." Mazur was a 2021 third-round draft pick of the Wings, who appeared on the cusp of making the NHL full-time several times but was always held back by a series of unfortunate injuries. Mazur always has been a high-energy, pesky winger who could play a physical, hard game but also had a good scoring touch in college and minor league hockey. But, oh, those injuries. In his NHL debut, in March 2025, Mazur suffered and elbow injury on his second shift of the game . He was unable to play the rest of the season with the Wings, or minor-league affiliate Grand Rapids. Injuries marred Mazur's last season, also, but when he got healthy in Grand Rapids, Mazur (Jackson/Jackson Lumen Christi) was recalled by the Wings and played in eight games in the schedule's late portion. More: Ron Duguay, former Red Wings forward, dies at age 69 Mazur finally got his first NHL point this season, an assist, and is getting ice time in a bottom-six forward, checking role the Wings' envisioned him being in. "It's a lot of getting used to things," Mazur said of being in the NHL. "Getting used to the travel, a lot of things. But I'm feeling pretty comfortable out there. It's just a matter of keep doing what I can to help the team win games and get points (for the standings)." Like so many young players entering any professional sports league, being in and out the lineup and playing more of a non-offensive role is different for Mazur, who scored a high of 22 goals collegiately at Denver and topped out at 17 in a season in Grand Rapids. But Mazur is adapting to the newer responsibilities "It's a different thing but, again, you have to learn from it and grow from it," Mazur said. "It's a different league, a different beast for sure here. I've played in four games this season and I'm getting comfortable with every game. The more I play and the more I'm going out there, I'm feeling better." Ice chips The Wings were expected to recall goaltender Michal Postava from Grand Rapids, as one of their NHL goaltenders was dealing with an injury and illness. Daniil Tarasov looked uncomfortable in Tuesday's shootout, after overtime, doing more stretching and bending after extending with his lower-body to make a save. ... J.T. Compher (undisclosed injury) was expected to return Thursday, Oct. 22, in Vancouver. Compher has practiced fully the last several days and McClellan was optimistic Compher would be ready to rejoin the lineup. Compher has only played the first two games of the season. ...If Compher were to play, McLellan said the Wings would return to a 12-forward/six-defensemen lineup. item.title: Mary Hardin-Baylor authors runaway victory at Golfweek October Classic
item.description: As Jackie Ralston’s team was pulling away from the field in the final round of the Golfweek October Classic, the veteran coach at Mary Hardin-Baylor fought the urge to add a little something. “I really kind of kept my mouth shut,” Ralston said when asked what her message to the team was amidst a 30-shot victory. “Sometimes as a coach you have that desire to want to put a little more info into it or encourage them in a certain way but I really felt like my group didn’t really need that from me at the moment but just to let them be them.” Mary Hardin-Baylor prevailed for the first time in the 15-year history of the Golfweek October Classic. They finished 54 holes at the Links Golf Club at Sandestin in Destin, Florida, with a 25-over total, which was 30 shots better than Macalester College. That was also a 54-hole program scoring record for the Crusaders. On the individual leaderboard, four Mary Hardin-Baylor players placed in the top 4, with Katie Rhude finishing solo second, Camryn Kiser solo third and Julia Sosa and Claire Smith tied for fourth. Huntingdon College’s Yvette Gorden claimed the individual title at even par, which gave her a five-shot edge on Rhude. Ralston attributes her team’s exceptional scoring in part to the work her players have put in so far this fall. Mary Hardin-Baylor came to Florida after playing the Tempest Golf Club in Longview, Texas, and competed at Nemacolin Resort in Farmington, Pennsylvania, before that. They took valuable lessons from each. Ralston thinks those starts helped her players learn what they’re capable of – especially when putts start dropping. “I was pleased when I was watching the scoreboard and seeing all that red go up,” Ralston said of the Golfweek event. “Just stay out of the way and let them do what they do and be available should somebody hit a wall or need some advice here or there.” Mary Hardin-Baylor led the field in par-4 and par-5 scoring as well as birdies. Victory at the Golfweek October Classic marked the Crusaders’ third team title in their five fall starts. Now that the first half of the season is over, Ralston said they’ll celebrate by getting the whole team together at their on-campus golf facility, theJane and Mac Hickerson Crusader Golf Club. The facility, which was dedicated a year ago, not only offers a place for the Crusader men’s and women’s teams to bond, but has been a gamechanger for practice. It includes a four-hole practice course with 23 tee boxes, a lighted short game area with two bunkers, a clubhouse and a hitting bay area with two Trackman units and a SAM PuttLab. Ben Crenshaw and Earl Santee, a well-known sports venue architect, designed the facility, named after Mac Hickerson, the first golf coach at Mary Hardin-Baylor. “ It’s like a kid in a candy store,” Ralston said of the place, which is solely for the use of the Mary Hardin-Baylor golf teams. item.title: Is the Flyers Youth Injection Making Veterans Expendable?
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The future of the Philadelphia Flyers has been on full display. We have already seen what players like Matvei Michkov and Trevor Zegras are capable of. Porter Martone dominated upon his arrival in Philadelphia, and is finding that form again. Denver Barkey and Alex Bump both played pivotal roles during last season’s playoff push. Barkey himself has continued to be a key player for the Flyers in 2026-27. Then, you have guys like Oliver Bonk and Cole Knuble who were called up due to injury issues with the team and are making the absolute best impressions they can. With the addition of guys like Bonk, Bump, and Knuble, the Flyers lineup is as young as ever. That’s partially because they’ve been without veterans Cam York, Rasmus Ristolainen, Travis Konency, and Owen Tippett. When starting the season at full health (regarding the starting 23, anyway), the Flyers went on a downward spiral to open up regular-season play. The injury bug started to hit, with the Flyers losing Ristolainen, then York, Konecny, and Tippett all to injury. Losing 4 key players is usually no way for a team to snap out of a funk. However, that “next man up” mentality kicked in. Knowing what they were missing, the then-winless Flyers knew they had a tough task at hand. Fast forward to Thursday, the Flyers are celebrating their 3rd consecutive win. They’ve done it with the injection of youth seen in the lineup. When the team gets healthy, they’ll have some tough choices to make. Do you send Cole Knuble back to the AHL, who, after just 2 games, is tied for the 3rd-most goals on the team? Or what about Oliver Bonk, who has been playing like a legitimate top-pair defenseman since assuming the role? The Martone-Cates-Michkov line has been creating more offense than any other Flyers line. Do you limit their minutes once the vets are healthy? Denver Barkey, again, has been such a utility tool for the Flyers, and though he has not scored yet, Alex Bump’s shot remains something that the Flyers need in the lineup. All of the young guys bring something to the table, and it’s working. There is an energy around the team that was lacking earlier in the year. Before Cole Knuble took his picture with his first goal puck, Trevor Zegras came in, grabbed it, then started yelling “get everybody”. Knuble’s teammates then starting cheering while he was talking to us, excitedly waiting to take the photo. — Will James (@wmjsports) October 22, 2026 Maybe that comes from winning. Or maybe the Flyers are feeling the energy from the youthful injection. Trevor Zegras on the Bump-Barkey-Knuble line: “Not a lot of brain cells” “They're great. Bring a lot of energy for the team in the locker room, on the bench. They're having a blast, which goes up and down the line up.” — Will James (@wmjsports) October 20, 2026 So, that raises the question: does the emergence of the Flyers’ youth make the veterans expendable? Read More: James: Flyers Need to Keep Oliver Bonk in Top-Pair Role,
item.content:encoded: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The future of the Philadelphia Flyers has been on full display. We have already seen what players like Matvei Michkov and Trevor Zegras are capable of. Porter Martone dominated upon his arrival in Philadelphia, and is finding that form again. Denver Barkey and Alex Bump both played pivotal roles during last season’s playoff push. Barkey himself has continued to be a key player for the Flyers in 2026-27. Then, you have guys like Oliver Bonk and Cole Knuble who were called up due to injury issues with the team and are making the absolute best impressions they can. With the addition of guys like Bonk, Bump, and Knuble, the Flyers lineup is as young as ever. That’s partially because they’ve been without veterans Cam York, Rasmus Ristolainen, Travis Konency, and Owen Tippett. When starting the season at full health (regarding the starting 23, anyway), the Flyers went on a downward spiral to open up regular-season play. The injury bug started to hit, with the Flyers losing Ristolainen, then York, Konecny, and Tippett all to injury. Losing 4 key players is usually no way for a team to snap out of a funk. However, that “next man up” mentality kicked in. Knowing what they were missing, the then-winless Flyers knew they had a tough task at hand. Fast forward to Thursday, the Flyers are celebrating their 3rd consecutive win. They’ve done it with the injection of youth seen in the lineup. When the team gets healthy, they’ll have some tough choices to make. Do you send Cole Knuble back to the AHL, who, after just 2 games, is tied for the 3rd-most goals on the team? Or what about Oliver Bonk, who has been playing like a legitimate top-pair defenseman since assuming the role? The Martone-Cates-Michkov line has been creating more offense than any other Flyers line. Do you limit their minutes once the vets are healthy? Denver Barkey, again, has been such a utility tool for the Flyers, and though he has not scored yet, Alex Bump’s shot remains something that the Flyers need in the lineup. All of the young guys bring something to the table, and it’s working. There is an energy around the team that was lacking earlier in the year. Before Cole Knuble took his picture with his first goal puck, Trevor Zegras came in, grabbed it, then started yelling “get everybody”. Knuble’s teammates then starting cheering while he was talking to us, excitedly waiting to take the photo. — Will James (@wmjsports) October 22, 2026 Maybe that comes from winning. Or maybe the Flyers are feeling the energy from the youthful injection. Trevor Zegras on the Bump-Barkey-Knuble line: “Not a lot of brain cells” “They're great. Bring a lot of energy for the team in the locker room, on the bench. They're having a blast, which goes up and down the line up.” — Will James (@wmjsports) October 20, 2026 So, that raises the question: does the emergence of the Flyers’ youth make the veterans expendable? Read More: James: Flyers Need to Keep Oliver Bonk in Top-Pair Role, Even Once Back to Full Strength Does the Flyers Youth Injection Make the Veterans Expendable? We’ve all heard about the Flyers’ logjam on the wing. It’s been a recurring topic of conversation for several summers, and really became prevalent last season with the early arrivals of Bump, Barkey, and even Martone (though I would not say his was early). The Flyers are loaded up on the wing. They have Travis Konecny, Tyson Foerster, and Owen Tippett, all joining Zegras (if he becomes a full-time winger), Michkov, and Martone as wingers who need to be in top-6 roles. That’s 6 right there, and there are only 4 spots in the top-6. Then you have Barkey, Bump, and Knuble, all of whom are strong 3rd line candidates. They’re so loaded on the wing that one of them will have to be on the 4th line. But now, Oliver Bonk’s sudden emergence has created a new blockage: right-side defense. Once healthy, the Flyers will have Bonk, Ristolainen, Jamie Drysdale, and David Jiricek as right-side defensemen. But that also goes to the power play too, as Bonk could be competing for minutes against Drysdale, Jiricek, and Cam York. Hunter McDonald, though it has not been Bonk-level of impressive, has looked like a decent 3rd-pair guy as well. Owen Tippett’s speed is always missed when the winger is out. While Knuble does not bring the same power shot or physicality, he makes up for it with finesse while matching the speed. Rasmus Ristolainen is a really strong defensive blueliner, but Bonk is showing similar defensive instincts early on, all while adding more offense. Not to mention, Bonk’s power play potential remains untapped. While he has historically played the bumper on the man-advantage, it’s hard not to imagine what he could do as a power-play QB given what he’s done from the point at 5-on-5, especially over the last two games. One veteran who I would still say should not become expendable is Travis Konecny. His leadership is still crucial to the team and is irreplaceable. It’s been a very small sample size, and that is something that needs to be kept in mind. Just because Bonk, Knuble, and Barkey are playing well, it does not mean the Flyers can freely go wheeling and dealing veterans who have been important to this team for a while. However, the recent success of the young guys certainly creates some intrigue. With the need for a true top-center and maybe even a top-4 defender still prevalent, it has to make you wonder if some veteran players may become more expendable if this level of success continues. Read More: The Necessary Spark: Cole Knuble Is Injecting Life Into the Flyers Lineup Read more at Philly Hockey Now

item.title: USMNT to face Haiti in Concacaf Nations League Quarterfinals
item.description: ARLINGTON, TX - JUNE 22: Haiti forward Ruben Providence (#18) dribble the ball in traffic during the Concacaf Gold Cup soccer match between the United States and Haiti on June 22, 2025 at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, TX. (Photo by Matthew Visinsky/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The United States Men’s National Team have had the first leg of the Concacaf Nations League Quarterfinals against Haiti moved to domestic soil. Today, Concacaf announced that it had approved a formal request by the Haitian Football Federation to move their home match, originally set to take place on November 14th at Sabina Park, to Nu Stadium in Miami. The match will still take place on November 14th as the first leg of the series, with Haiti serving as the home team. For years, Haiti has not been able to host matches on home soil due to the political unrest that continues within the country. During the group stage of the Concacaf Nations League earlier this month, Haiti played their two home matches at Sabina Park, Jamaica’s national cricket stadium, in Kingston. Immediately after the group stage concluded, Concacaf announced that stadium would once again serve as Haiti’s home field against the USMNT, a match which would have taken place just hours before Jamaica hosted Mexico at Independence Park just a couple of miles down the road. Now, the match will take place in Miami, which has a large Haitian-American population that the Haitian federation hopes will come out to support them in that crucial opening leg. MATCH UPDATE: @Concacaf announced it has approved the request of the Haitian Football Federation to move the first leg of our Nations League quarterfinal from Kingston, Jamaica to Nu Stadium in Miami, FL. The second leg will still take place as scheduled in Cincinnati on 11/17. pic.twitter.com/OsahrTWPnd — U.S. Soccer Men's National Team (@USMNT) October 22, 2026 The second leg of the quarterfinals will still take place at TQL Stadium in Cincinnati on November 17th. The USMNT designated that stadium for their home leg in September and the details of that match remain unchanged. Now, the USMNT will have both legs on domestic soil and will play in Nu Stadium for the first time since it opened earlier this year.

item.title: Bruno’s betrayal? ‘Toxic’ Fernandes is symptom of United’s culture of entitlement | Jamie Jackson
item.description: Michael Carrick must now deal with more dressing-room unrest after Lisandro Martínez’s attack on the board “Toxic”: this is the damning characterisation of Bruno Fernandes from one highly placed Manchester United source after the captain’s incendiary betrayal of Michael Carrick. There has surely never been a greater anti-leadership act in United’s storied history than Fernandes questioning the man who trusts him to unify the dressing room and execute his on-field plan. The Portuguese has proved this faith wrong at the precise moment he was required to step up and exude a defiant togetherness. Continue reading...

item.title: Haiti move Nations League home clash with USA to Miami amid gang violence crisis
item.description: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US in South Florida on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage On Thursday, Concacaf announced that it had approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Initially, Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the United States, had been booked in Kingston. The Grenadiers had previously played their World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...
item.dc:creator: Jeff Rueter
item.content:encoded: Concacaf approves exceptional hosting arrangement Haiti to face US in South Florida on 14 November Miami’s Haitian community offers home advantage On Thursday, Concacaf announced that it had approved Haiti’s request to relocate their Nations League quarter-final first leg on 14 November from Kingston, Jamaica, to Miami in an “exceptional hosting arrangement”. Haiti have been unable to play nominal “home” games within their borders since July 2021, with the United Nations estimating that 90% of Port-au-Prince – including the national stadium – is controlled by violent gangs. Initially, Haiti’s match, the first leg of a home-and-away series against the United States, had been booked in Kingston. The Grenadiers had previously played their World Cup qualifiers in Curaçao, Aruba and Barbados. However, the Nations League format slated Curaçao and Jamaica to host their matches on the same night as Haiti’s, shunting Haiti to Sabina Park, the home of the Jamaica national team until their current venue opened in 1962. Now a cricket ground, Sabina Park hosted two of Haiti’s Nations League qualifiers. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Post-Ferguson worn-out horror show continues at Manchester United
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! We’re in the midst of what the kids call “spooky season” – or, for our fellow fusty old-timers out there, “autumn”. If you’ve been cosying up with a few horror flicks this month, you’ll know nothing good can come from hanging around a lake at this time of year. And so it proved for Manchester United, who endured an early Halloween nightmare on the banks of Lake Como that may have driven a stake through the Michael Carrick era. Hailed as the interim anti-Amorim not so long ago, Carrick has overseen two wins this season, against Ipswich and Sabah Baku . Como were in Serie D when Carrick won Big Cup with United as a player in 2008 – now, 18 years on, he watched the Italian upstarts dance, twirl and shimmy through the set of training cones he had sent out to represent his storied club. Any chance the Independent Football Regulator could also force the sale of Manchester United while it is at it? – James Marriott. Belated birthday greetings to Florent Sinama-Pongolle, a player once described (by Big Website if memory serves) as the only footballer whose surname sounds like an art-house trend – Alan Burgess. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. To get the full version, just visit this page and follow the instructions . Continue reading...

item.title: Trump’s Fifa peace prize was a sham. A reimagined award can still have meaning | Leander Schaerlaeckens
item.description: The first awarding marked the apex of Gianni Infantino’s hubris. A new version could highlight the good in the world of soccer Sign up for our free newsletter here Poor Fifa peace prize. Unloved, unliked, mocked, tainted by association with its first winner. And now demoted, too, after Fifa’s president, Gianni Infantino, dumped the thing on the global governing body’s “social responsibility committee” to look after. To redeem it, rather than to ditch it, to spare Infantino the embarrassment of acknowledging that his fake prize was really just a fake prize all along. Here is where we should probably acknowledge that, as fake prizes go, and in the context of what it was intended to accomplish, the first awarding of the Fifa peace prize was an unqualified success. It achieved exactly what it was meant to, made by Infantino to flatter Donald Trump, the man he needed to keep on his side to safeguard the riches to be extracted from the North American market in order to consolidate his power base within Fifa. Trump, the gullible buffoon, was pleased as punch – handed a big, golden bauble and a medal he placed around his own neck – and briefly forgot about the Nobel peace prize he desperately covets . Leander Schaerlaeckens is the author of The Long Game: US Men’s Soccer and Its Savage, Four-Decade Journey to the Top, or Thereabouts, which is out now . He teaches at Marist University. Continue reading...

item.title: Carrick joins Wilcox under the bus after Manchester United’s latest night in crisis | Max Rushden
item.description: Bruno Fernandes followed Lisandro Martínez in revolt after his team’s 4-1 defeat to Como in the Champions League You have to credit Manchester United. Your local rivals have turned the Premier League into an almost meaningless farce. We are questioning the validity of anything we’ve seen over the past 20 years; wondering how many goals Erling Haaland will get in the Championship. We are looking at the league table from second position down and wishing we’d invested in inflatable bananas a month ago. And yet here comes the Old Trafford machine: from players to the captain to the manager to the director of football, to the director of the director of football, to a minority owner who feels the UK is being “colonised by immigrants” , to debt-leveraging majority owners who take vast sums out of the club and are collectively saying hold my Ineos-sponsored high-performance wellness immune boost smoothie. Continue reading...

item.title: Bruno Guimarães had sleepless nights before Newcastle exit but hopes for same ‘love’ at Arsenal
item.description: Midfielder says there were a lot of tears as he said goodbye at St James’ Park but he is enjoying the remorselessness at his new club For Bruno Guimarães, it was a time to show his steeliness, to fix his eyes on the prize – even if he knew it would surely mean them welling up. And then some. It was a tumultuous summer for the Brazil midfielder. A fine World Cup on a personal level was marred by a crucial penalty miss in the last-16 loss against Norway . Now he had the dream move lined up to Arsenal but it could not happen without breaking some hearts at Newcastle. Guimarães admits he lay awake at night as the emotions swirled. How could he leave Newcastle, the club where he made so many connections and enjoyed so many highs after joining from Lyon in January 2022? There were the Champions League qualifications and, above all, the Carabao Cup triumph in 2025 that ended a 70-year wait for a domestic trophy. On the other hand, how could he resist Arsenal and the prospect of competing regularly for the game’s top honours? Continue reading...

item.title: Nottingham Forest’s false start places early focus on Glasner and Delap
item.description: Austrian’s tactics need adapting to but Forest are in the bottom three and their owner is not the patient type Sitting 19th in the Premier League was not the plan for Nottingham Forest after the arrival of a highly acclaimed manager and a £45m striker to fuel their ambitions. The fates of Oliver Glasner and Liam Delap are intertwined and with the stark stats of zero home goals and a solitary point at the City Ground it is not the dream start they were aiming for. As Delap prepares to return to Ipswich, where his career ignited, on Friday night, Forest are remaining calm. There is a desperation to get away from the short-termism that caused so many problems; 12 months ago, they were on their third head coach of a disappointing season. This summer they were ruthless with the removal of Vítor Pereira, who had done a fine job to escape the drop, because they saw an opportunity to upgrade with Glasner, hoping he could transform Forest like he did Crystal Palace. Continue reading...

item.description: Norwegian forward might look to Harry Kane for inspiration on the pitch, but when north London derby comes around, she needs no lessons on what the rivalry means “It means more than just three points. It’s for the whole club. It’s for the whole place. It’s for the whole of Tottenham.” One only needs to be in the presence of Tottenham Hotspur’s Cathinka Tandberg for a few minutes to feel the passion that emanates from her when it comes to this weekend’s north London derby. As a lifelong Spurs fan, the forward understands more than most the intensity of the rivalry that exists between her side and Arsenal, one that she cannot wait to experience once again on Saturday. “It will just be an incredible feeling,” she tells Moving the Goalposts. “I think you will feel a few nerves that you maybe don’t feel in a normal game but that’s good.” Continue reading...

item.title: Harry Kane admits wait to learn if he has won Ballon d’Or is ‘very stressful’ for family
item.description: Bayern Munich and England striker is odds-on favourite ‘I try not to think about it. Obviously it is hard not to’ Harry Kane would love to know now whether he has won the Ballon d’Or because the uncertainty and constant questions are driving his family to distraction. But the Bayern Munich and England striker accepts the suspense before the big reveal at the London Palladium on Monday night is part of the show. Kane is the odds-on favourite to win the prestigious individual honour after a prolific run of form. The 33-year-old scored 61 goals for Bayern last season and 12 for England. This time out, he has 10 for Bayern and six for England. He scored from the penalty spot in Wednesday night’s 2-2 Champions League draw against Arsenal at the Allianz Arena, although his standout moment was the inch-perfect through ball that set up Alphonso Davies to make it 1-1. Continue reading...

item.title: Barkley and Buendía on target as Aston Villa sink Viking to maintain perfect start
item.description: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. Perhaps Villa really will rekindle the spirit of 1982 but the frustration here, albeit minor in the wider scheme, was that they could not maintain their bird’s-eye view over the continent. A superbly taken volley by Peter Christiansen, awarded by the video assistant referee after initially being disallowed for offside, gave Viking a consolation their second-half display deserved and meant Unai Emery’s side must make do with slumming it just behind Paris Saint-Germain. Continue reading...

item.title: ‘We can go all the way’: Jonas Eidevall on life at San Diego Wave and lessons learned from Arsenal
item.description: The Swede’s team are second in the NWSL and hope to create special memories at their Snapdragon Stadium “I love the ocean,” Jonas Eidevall says, and he references walks along the beach at Del Mar. “People are very relaxed, life is lived at a slower pace here. I’m a very simple person. I like to read a book, go to the gym and spend time with my wife and kids, that’s sort of all I need.” The former Arsenal head coach is revelling in a calmer world as the head coach of San Diego Wave but it is not merely the beaches that are lowering his stress levels; his team are on a five-game winning streak in the NWSL and sit second in the table, one point off top spot, with two matches to go before the playoffs. Winning feels good and the club are targeting silverware, as he tells the Guardian: “It would mean everything. There are no guarantees in the playoffs, but the exciting part is saying: ‘We can also go all the way’ – that’s a possibility for us and we need to believe.” Continue reading...

item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Does anyone feature on more than two clubs' all-time top-10 scoring charts? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the longest kit supply partnerships, more own goals (part II) and consecutive goalless draws Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Harry Kane is now Bayern’s seventh-highest scorer of all time, as well as being Tottenham’s highest scorer. The man he overtook at the top of that list, Jimmy Greaves, is also Chelsea’s seventh-highest scorer of all time. Do any other players feature on two (or more) clubs’ all-time top- 10 scoring charts?” asks Owen Powell. A trawl through the Knowledge archive reminded us that we have previously looked at players who are the record goalscorer for more than one club . This question is slightly different, as we’re focusing on goalscorers who are in the all-time top 10 for the most different clubs. There are dozens of players who appear for two clubs, including Sergio Ag üero (Atlético Madrid and Manchester City), Kenny Dalglish (Celtic and Liverpool), Jimmy Greaves (Chelsea and Tottenham) , Lionel Messi (Barcelona and Inter Miami), Cristiano Ronaldo (Real Madrid and Al-Nassr) and Alan Shearer (Blackburn and Newcastle). Continue reading...

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.title: Dwight Yorke: ‘I’m not a kid trying to get into management – I’m a manager’
item.description: Ghana may soon come calling for Trinidad and Tobago’s former captain and manager, who is proud of his CV since his days as a Premier League striker Dwight Yorke wants you to stop calling him a former player. “I’m not a kid trying to get into management for the first time,” he says from his home in Dubai. “I’ve done that and I want that message to come across clearly.” The message has a deadline. Carlos Queiroz left his job as Ghana head coach on 1 October and the Ghana Football Association is searching for his successor. Yorke is among the names under consideration, along with Pape Thiaw, Aliou Cissé and Walid Regragui, the former Morocco head coach, according to Ghanaian media. Continue reading...

item.title: Houdini act in Venice leaves Massimiliano Allegri searching for an escape at Napoli | Nicky Bandini
item.description: Manager’s latest setback exposed growing doubts about his squad and his approach as Davide Nicola began his Venezia tenure with a remarkable win “I’ll love you even if you win,” promised the Venezia supporter’s banner. More gallows humour from a fanbase that proved long ago that its relationship with the club could survive a defeat. They had endured six already in the first six rounds of this Serie A season: the only team in the division without a win or even a single point. The last time they were in Serie A, in 2024-25, Venezia finished 19th. The time before that, in 2021-22, they finished bottom. Deja vu all over again? A 3-1 defeat by Atalanta in the first game back after this month’s international break pushed Venezia to breaking point. The club fired the manager Giovanni Stroppa, who had led them to the Serie B title and promotion the previous season. Continue reading...

item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 talking points from the weekend’s action
item.description: Florian Wirtz takes on more responsibility in Liverpool’s attack while Pierre Sage is under pressure at Crystal Palace Dominic Calvert-Lewin’s physicality overpowering Bryan Mbeumo in Manchester United’s area at a corner grabbed him a fifth goal in 10 outings for Leeds: a pretty respectable ratio. “I just tried to cause a ruckus,” said Leeds’ No 9. “I make it difficult for the defender. I read the flight of the ball and was quickest to react. I feel really comfortable [here]. I feel the support from the club and the fans and it is a great feeling stepping on to the pitch, particularly at Elland Road.” Of the contenders to be understudy to Harry Kane as England’s centre-forward, Calvert-Lewin may be the lead act – if he can stay injury-free, which has been a difficulty throughout his career. item.title: Elite-level incompetence is Manchester United’s problem – not Michael Carrick | Barney Ronay
item.description: Getting rid of head coach is not going to solve the problems that led to his appointment. Perhaps it’s worth, for once, doing something different At the final whistle at Elland Road the TV cameras cut to a lingering shot of the Manchester United chief executive, Omar Berrada, looking down pensively from the stands, deciding, it is to be hoped, on a little clemency, a re-sheathing of the managerial shotgun. Here we have the man who hired the man. The man who fires the man. The man who also hired or rehired the previous two men he had to fire. Berrada was poached from Manchester City on the basis of his ability to grow commercial revenue (yes, OK, stop laughing), and appears, like everyone else with any actual reach around here, to exist in a strangely consequence-free bubble. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Martínez has drawn back the curtain on Manchester United’s ruinous ownership | Jonathan Liew
item.description: Defender may not be blameless in team’s struggles but his criticism goes to the heart of what has gone wrong at the club Heartbreaking: the worst defender you know just made a great point. And no, nobody would describe Lisandro Martínez as the ideal person to scrutinise Manchester United’s indifferent start to the season , given that his high-profile defensive errors against Fulham and Tottenham are partly responsible for it. “We’re all trying to find the guy who did this,” Martínez burbles on Amazon Prime after United’s 2-0 defeat by Atlético Madrid on Tuesday night, dressed in a hot dog costume and throwing his arms out in mock innocence. For those with no interest in engaging with what Martínez actually had to say, this alone will be sufficient grounds to ignore him. Already you can sense the squeamishness of former players for whom the violation of an omertà is the real cardinal sin here, a phantom limb that still tingles years after they last stepped into a dressing room. “Disrespectful,” reckoned Wayne Rooney. “I don’t feel like he’s got the right,” agreed Ashley Young. “These things don’t end well, man,” Rio Ferdinand observed on his podcast. Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Continue reading...

item.title: Transfer window verdict: how every Premier League club fared
item.description: The British transfer record was equalled and one club signed no fewer than 18 players in another hectic summer Bringing in Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa was a strong start to the window but could Arsenal’s failure to sign a marquee attacker cost them in the long run? They began targeting Morgan Rogers before pivoting to Vinícius Júnior when the England forward went to Chelsea, only to end up disappointed when Vinícius signed a new deal with Real Madrid. Julián Alvarez made clear he had no intention of joining from Atlético Madrid in the final days of the window and Arsenal kept their powder dry despite sanctioning the exits of Gabriel Jesus to Barcelona and Ethan Nwaneri to Borussia Dortmund. Should Gabriel Martinelli complete his move to Al-Hilal as expected in the coming days – the Saudi Pro League window remains open – a few injuries could leave Arteta short. Ed Aarons Continue reading...

item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...

item.title: Aitana Bonmatí makes Guardian top 100 history with third title in a row
item.description: The margin may have got smaller but the brilliant Spanish midfielder makes it a hat-trick of No 1 finishes They say the best things come in threes, and Aitana Bonmatí has written herself into the Guardian’s top 100 history as the first player to finish at the top of the tree for a third consecutive year. Last year the majestic midfielder emulated her Barcelona and Spain teammate Alexia Putellas by winning for a second year running , but the 27-year-old has now gone one better, establishing herself once again at the top of the women’s game. Continue reading...
